title.en: Volume 133 Biographies 71: Pan Chen, Zhang Jue son: Jinyan, Ye Luyudu, Wo Wo
title.raw: 卷一百三十三 列傳第七十一: 叛臣 張覺子:僅言 耶律餘睹 窩斡 Volume 133 Biographies 71: Pan Chen, Zhang Jue son: Jinyan, Ye Luyudu, Wo Wo

sentences.zh: 古書「畔」與「叛」通，畔之為言界也。

translations.literal: In ancient books, the character pan (畔) and pan (叛, "rebel") are interchangeable; the meaning of pan is "boundary."
translations.idiomatic: In classical texts, the characters for pan (boundary) and pan (rebel) are used interchangeably; etymologically, pan denotes a boundary.

sentences.zh: 《左氏》曰，政猶「農之有畔」，是也。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary says, "Government is like a farmer having boundaries"—that is the point.
translations.idiomatic: As the Zuo Commentary puts it: governing a state is like farming a field—one must keep clear boundaries.

sentences.zh: 君臣上下之定分，猶此疆彼界之截然，違此向彼，即為叛矣。

translations.literal: The fixed roles of ruler and minister, superior and inferior, are like boundaries sharply divided between this side and that; to cross from one side to the other is rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The proper hierarchy between ruler and subject is as sharply drawn as a border between fields; to step across that line is treason.

sentences.zh: 善惡判于跬步，禍患極於懷襄，吁，可畏哉！

translations.literal: Good and evil are decided within a single step; calamity reaches its height at the time of the Great Flood—alas, how fearsome!
translations.idiomatic: A single misstep can decide one's fate between good and evil, and disaster can swell to flood-tide proportions—how terrifying!

sentences.zh: 作《叛臣傳》。

translations.literal: Therefore I compose the "Biographies of Traitors."
translations.idiomatic: Hence this "Biographies of Traitors."

sentences.zh: 張覺，亦書作鐧，平州義豐人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jue (also written as Jian) was a native of Yifeng in Ping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jue (also written Jian) was from Yifeng in Ping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 在遼第進士，仕至遼興軍節度副使。

translations.literal: He placed first in the Liao jinshi examination and served as far as vice military commissioner of Liaoxing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He took first place in the Liao jinshi examination and rose to vice military commissioner of Liaoxing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 太祖定燕京，時立愛以平州降，當時宋人以海上之盟求燕京及西京地，太祖以燕京、涿、易、檀、順、景、薊與之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizu secured Yanjing, Shi Liai surrendered Ping Prefecture. At that time the Song, invoking the maritime alliance, sought Yanjing and the Western Capital territories; the emperor gave them Yanjing, Zhuo, Yi, Tan, Shun, Jing, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Taizu took Yanjing, Shi Liai surrendered Ping Prefecture. The Song, citing the maritime alliance, demanded Yanjing and the Western Capital lands; Taizu ceded Yanjing along with Zhuo, Yi, Tan, Shun, Jing, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 平州自入契丹別為一軍，故弗與，而以平州為南京，覺為留守。

translations.literal: Ping Prefecture, since entering Khitan control, had been a separate army district, so it was not included; instead Ping was made the Southern Capital, and Jue was appointed resident commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Ping Prefecture had long been a separate military district under the Khitan, so it was withheld; Ping was made the Southern Capital instead, with Jue as resident commissioner.

sentences.zh: 既而聞覺有異志，上遣使劉彥宗及斜缽諭之，詔曰：「平山一郡今為南京，節度使今為留守。

translations.literal: Learning that Jue harbored disloyal intentions, the emperor sent Liu Yanzong and Xiebo to admonish him, issuing an edict: "The single commandery of Pingshan is now the Southern Capital; the military commissioner is now the resident commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Jue harbored rebellious designs, the emperor sent Liu Yanzong and Xiebo to warn him with an edict: "The commandery of Pingshan is now the Southern Capital, and the post of military commissioner is now resident commissioner.

sentences.zh: 恩亦厚矣。

translations.literal: My grace toward you is already ample.
translations.idiomatic: My favor toward you is already generous.

sentences.zh: 或言汝等陰有異圖，何為當此農時輒相扇動，非去危就安之計也。

translations.literal: Some say you secretly harbor other designs—why, at the height of the farming season, do you stir unrest among the people? This is no plan for leaving danger and seeking safety.
translations.idiomatic: Some report that you secretly plot rebellion—why, in the middle of the planting season, do you incite unrest? That is no way to escape danger and find security.

sentences.zh: 其諭朕意。

translations.literal: Make known to them Our intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Convey Our meaning to them.

sentences.zh: 」太祖每收城邑，往往徙其民以實京師，民心多不安，故時立愛因降表曾言及之。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Taizu took a city, he often relocated its populace to populate the capital; popular sentiment was often unsettled, and so in his surrender memorial Shi Liai had once raised this concern.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Taizu captured a city, he often relocated its people to fill the capital, leaving the populace uneasy—Shi Liai had raised this very concern in his surrender memorial.

sentences.zh: 及以燕京與宋而遷其人，獨以空城與之，遷者道出平州，故覺因之以作亂。

translations.literal: When Yanjing was given to the Song and its people relocated, the Song received only an empty city; the evacuees passed through Ping Prefecture, and Jue used this occasion to raise rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanjing was handed to the Song and its inhabitants relocated, the Song received only an empty city; the evacuees passed through Ping Prefecture, and Jue seized the moment to rebel.

sentences.zh: 天輔七年五月，左企弓、虞仲文、曹勇義、康公弼赴廣甯，過平州，覺使人殺之于栗林下，遂據南京叛入于宋，宋人納之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year of Tianfu, Zuo Qigong, Yu Zhongwen, Cao Yongyi, and Kang Gongbi were traveling to Guangning and passed through Ping; Jue had them killed under the chestnut grove, seized the Southern Capital, defected to the Song, and the Song accepted him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Tianfu 7 (1123), Zuo Qigong, Yu Zhongwen, Cao Yongyi, and Kang Gongbi were en route to Guangning and passed through Ping; Jue had them murdered in a chestnut grove, seized the Southern Capital, defected to the Song, and was welcomed by them.

sentences.zh: 太祖下詔諭南京官吏，詔曰：「朕初駐蹕燕京，嘉爾吏民率先降附，故升府治以為南京，減徭役，薄賦稅，恩亦至矣，何苦輒為叛逆？

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu issued an edict to admonish the officials of the Southern Capital: "When I first halted at Yanjing, I praised your officials and people for surrendering first; therefore I elevated the prefecture to be the Southern Capital, reduced corvée labor, and lightened taxes—My grace has been complete. Why must you suffer yourselves to rebel?
translations.idiomatic: Taizu issued an edict to the officials of the Southern Capital: "When I first encamped at Yanjing, I commended your officials and people for being the first to submit; I elevated your prefecture to the Southern Capital, eased corvée duties, and reduced taxes—My kindness has been ample. Why court rebellion?

sentences.zh: 今欲進兵攻取，時方農月，不忍以一惡人而害及眾庶。

translations.literal: Now I wish to advance troops to attack and seize it, but it is the farming season; I cannot bear to harm the multitude because of one wicked man.
translations.idiomatic: I am ready to march and take the city by force, but it is planting season, and I cannot bear to harm the common people for the sake of one villain.

sentences.zh: 且遼國舉為我有，孤城自守，終欲何為？

translations.literal: Moreover, the entire Liao state has become Mine; what can a lone city holding out by itself ultimately hope to achieve?
translations.idiomatic: The whole Liao realm is already mine—what can a lone city hope to accomplish by holding out?

sentences.zh: 今止坐首惡，餘並釋之。」

translations.literal: Now I will punish only the chief culprit; all the rest shall be released."
translations.idiomatic: I will punish only the ringleader and release all the rest."

sentences.zh: 覺兵五萬屯潤州近郊，欲脅遷、來、潤、隰四州。

translations.literal: Jue's army of fifty thousand encamped in the suburbs of Run Prefecture, intending to coerce the four prefectures of Qian, Lai, Run, and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Jue stationed fifty thousand troops in the suburbs of Run Prefecture, aiming to intimidate Qian, Lai, Run, and Xi into submission.

sentences.zh: 闍母自錦州往討之，已敗覺兵，欲乘勝攻南京，時暑雨不可進，退屯於海堧。

translations.literal: Chamu's forces came from Jinzhou to attack him; he had already defeated Jue's army and wished to press the advantage to attack the Southern Capital, but summer rains made advance impossible, so he withdrew and encamped at Haichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chamu marched from Jinzhou to suppress him, routed Jue's forces, and tried to press on to the Southern Capital, but summer rains blocked the advance; he withdrew to camp at Haichuan.

sentences.zh: 無何，闍母再敗覺兵，復與戰於兔耳山，闍母大敗，覺報捷于宋。

translations.literal: Before long Chamu again defeated Jue's army; they fought again at Rabbit-Ear Mountain, and Chamu suffered a great defeat; Jue reported victory to the Song.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chamu defeated Jue again, but at Rabbit-Ear Mountain Chamu himself was routed; Jue sent word of victory to the Song.

sentences.zh: 宋建平州為泰寧軍，以覺為節度使，張敦固等皆加徽猶閣待制，以銀絹數萬犒軍。

translations.literal: The Song established Ping Prefecture as Taining Circuit, appointed Jue military commissioner, promoted Zhang Dun'gu and others to Huaiyou Pavilion attendant-in-waiting, and rewarded the army with tens of thousands in silver and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Song reorganized Ping Prefecture as Taining Circuit, made Jue its military commissioner, promoted Zhang Dun'gu and others to Huaiyou Pavilion attendant-in-waiting, and lavished tens of thousands in silver and silk on the troops.

sentences.zh: 宗望軍至南京城東，覺兵大敗宵遁，遂奔宋，入於燕京。

translations.literal: Zongwang's army reached the east of the Southern Capital; Jue's forces were utterly defeated and fled by night; he then fled to the Song and entered Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongwang's army reached the east gate of the Southern Capital, Jue's troops were routed and fled by night; he fled to the Song and took refuge in Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 宗望以納叛責宋宣撫司，索張覺。

translations.literal: Zongwang blamed the Song Pacification Commission for harboring a rebel and demanded Zhang Jue.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwang accused the Song Pacification Commission of sheltering a traitor and demanded Zhang Jue be handed over.

sentences.zh: 宣撫王安中匿之於甲仗庫，紿曰：「無之。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Wang Anzhong hid him in the armory and deceived them, saying, "He is not here.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Wang Anzhong hid him in the armory and lied: "We do not have him.

sentences.zh: 」宗望索愈急，安中乃斬貌類覺者一人當之，金人識之曰：「非覺也。

translations.literal: Zongwang's demands grew more urgent; Anzhong then beheaded a man who resembled Jue and offered him in his place; the Jurchens recognized him and said, "This is not Jue.
translations.idiomatic: As Zongwang pressed harder, Anzhong beheaded a look-alike and presented the head; the Jurchens recognized the deception: "This is not Jue.

sentences.zh: 」安中不得已，引覺出。

translations.literal: Anzhong had no choice but to produce Jue.
translations.idiomatic: With no alternative, Anzhong produced Jue.

sentences.zh: 數以罪，覺罵宋人不容口，遂殺覺函其首以與金人。

translations.literal: He enumerated his crimes; Jue cursed the Song without pause; they then killed Jue, boxed his head, and gave it to the Jurchens.
translations.idiomatic: After listing his crimes, Jue cursed the Song without cease; they executed him, boxed his head, and delivered it to the Jurchens.

sentences.zh: 燕京降將及常勝軍皆泣下，郭藥師自言曰：「若來索藥師當奈何？

translations.literal: The surrendered generals of Yanjing and the Ever-Victorious Army all wept; Guo Yaoshi said to himself, "If they come to demand Yaoshi, what then?
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered generals in Yanjing and the Ever-Victorious Army wept openly; Guo Yaoshi muttered, "If they come for me next, what then?

sentences.zh: 」自是，降將卒皆解體。

translations.literal: From this time, the surrendered generals and soldiers all lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: From that day on, surrendered officers and troops lost all morale.

sentences.zh: 及金人伐宋，竟以納平州之叛為執言雲。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens later attacked the Song, they ultimately used the sheltering of the Ping Prefecture rebel as their pretext.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens later invaded the Song, they cited the sheltering of the Ping Prefecture rebel as their casus belli.

sentences.zh: 子僅言。

translations.literal: His son Jinyan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jinyan.

sentences.zh: 子 僅言

translations.literal: Son: Jinyan
translations.idiomatic: Son: Jinyan

sentences.zh: 僅言幼名元奴。

translations.literal: Jinyan's childhood name was Yuannu.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyan's childhood name was Yuannu.

sentences.zh: 宗望攻下平山，僅言在繈褓間，裏人劉承宣得之，養於家。

translations.literal: When Zongwang captured Pingshan, Jinyan was still in swaddling clothes; a fellow townsman, Liu Chengxuan, took him in and raised him at home.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongwang took Pingshan, Jinyan was still an infant; a neighbor, Liu Chengxuan, found him and raised him in his household.

sentences.zh: 其鄰韓夫人甚愛之。

translations.literal: A neighbor, Lady Han, doted on him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor, Lady Han, adored him.

sentences.zh: 年數歲，因隨韓夫人得見貞懿皇后。

translations.literal: When he was several years old, he accompanied Lady Han to an audience with Empress Zhenyi.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of several years, he accompanied Lady Han to an audience with Empress Zhenyi.

sentences.zh: 留之籓邸，稍長，侍世宗讀書，遂使僅言主家事，繩檢部曲，一府憚之。

translations.literal: She kept him at the princely residence; as he grew older he attended Emperor Shizong in his studies; Shizong then had Jinyan manage household affairs and discipline the retainers—the entire mansion feared him.
translations.idiomatic: She kept him at the princely residence; as he grew up he studied with the future Emperor Shizong, who later put him in charge of household affairs and discipline over the retainers—the whole establishment stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 僅言能心計，世宗倚任之，凡宮室營造、府庫出納、行幸頓舍皆委之。

translations.literal: Jinyan was skilled in calculation; Shizong relied on him, entrusting to him all palace construction, treasury receipts and disbursements, and arrangements for imperial journeys and halts.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyan had a keen head for figures; Shizong relied on him for palace construction, treasury accounts, and all arrangements for imperial tours and encampments.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘗曰：「一經僅言，無不愜朕意者。

translations.literal: Shizong once said, "Once it passes through Jinyan, nothing fails to satisfy My mind.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong once remarked, "Once Jinyan has handled a matter, it never fails to please me.

sentences.zh: 」六年，提舉修內役事，役夫掘地得白金匿之，事覺，法當死，僅言責取其物與官，釋其罪。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he supervised inner-palace construction; laborers digging earth found white gold and concealed it; when the matter came to light the penalty was death, but Jinyan compelled them to surrender the goods to the state and released them from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he oversaw inner-palace construction; laborers unearthed hidden silver, a capital offense; Jinyan made them surrender the treasure to the state and spared their lives.

sentences.zh: 尋兼祗應司。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was additionally appointed to the Attendance Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon also appointed to the Attendance Office.

sentences.zh: 遷少府監，提控宮籍監、祗應司如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director of the Palace Workshops, continuing to oversee the Palace Registry Office and the Attendance Office as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Palace Workshops while retaining charge of the Palace Registry and Attendance offices.

sentences.zh: 護作太甯宮，引宮左流泉溉田，歲獲稻萬斛。

translations.literal: Supervising construction of the Taining Palace, he diverted the spring flowing to the left of the palace to irrigate fields, harvesting ten thousand piculs of rice per year.
translations.idiomatic: While supervising construction of Taining Palace, he channeled a spring west of the palace to irrigate fields, yielding ten thousand piculs of rice a year.

sentences.zh: 十七年，複提點內藏，典領昭德皇后山陵，遷勸農使，領諸職如故。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he again supervised the inner treasury, directed the mausoleum of Empress Zhaode, was promoted to commissioner for encouraging agriculture, and retained all his previous posts.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he again oversaw the inner treasury, directed Empress Zhaode's mausoleum, was promoted to commissioner for encouraging agriculture, and kept his other posts.

sentences.zh: 僅言雖舊臣，出入左右，然世宗終不假以權任。

translations.literal: Although Jinyan was an old retainer who attended him at his side, Shizong never entrusted him with real power.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jinyan was a longtime companion who attended him daily, Shizong never granted him real political authority.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，尚書省奏，宮苑司直長黎倫在職十六年，請與遷敘。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the Secretariat memorialized that Li Lun, chief clerk of the Palace Parks Office, had served sixteen years and requested promotion in rank.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 the Secretariat reported that Li Lun, chief clerk of the Palace Parks Office, had served sixteen years and sought a promotion.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此朕之家臣，質直人也，今已老矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "This is My household retainer, an honest and straightforward man, but he is old now.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "He is a household retainer of mine, honest and upright, but he is old now.

sentences.zh: 如勸農使張僅言亦朕舊臣，純實頗解事，凡朝廷議論，內外除授，未嘗得干預。

translations.literal: The Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture Zhang Jinyan is also an old retainer of Mine—sincere and quite capable—but in all court deliberations and appointments within and without, he has never been allowed to intervene.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Zhang Jinyan is another old retainer—sincere and capable—but he has never been permitted to meddle in court debates or appointments, internal or external.

sentences.zh: 朕觀自古人君為讒諂蒙蔽者多矣，朕雖不及古人，然近習憸言未嘗入耳。

translations.literal: I observe that since antiquity many rulers have been blinded by slander and flattery; though I do not equal the ancients, words of flattery from close attendants have never entered My ears.
translations.idiomatic: I know that many rulers throughout history were blinded by slander and flattery; I may not equal the ancients, but flattery from my intimates has never reached my ears.

sentences.zh: 」宰臣曰：「誠如聖訓，此國家之福也。

translations.literal: The chief ministers said, "Truly as Your sagely instruction states—this is the good fortune of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers replied, "As Your Majesty says—this is the state's good fortune.

sentences.zh: 」世宗欲以為橫海軍節度使，而不可去左右，遂止。

translations.literal: Shizong wished to appoint him military commissioner of Henghai Circuit, but could not bear to have him leave his side, and so desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong considered making him military commissioner of Henghai Circuit, but could not spare him from his side, and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 僅言始得疾，猶扶杖視事，疾亟，詔太醫診視，近侍問訊相屬。

translations.literal: When Jinyan first fell ill he still leaned on his staff to attend to duties; when the illness grew critical, an edict ordered imperial physicians to examine him, and close attendants came in succession to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinyan first fell ill he still attended to business with a staff in hand; as he worsened, imperial physicians were summoned and close attendants came one after another to inquire.

sentences.zh: 及卒，上深惜之，遣官致祭，賻銀五百兩、重彩十端、絹二百匹，棺槨、衣衾、銀汞、斂物、葬地皆官給，贈輔國上將軍。

translations.literal: When he died the emperor deeply mourned him, sent officials to offer sacrifices, granted five hundred taels of silver, ten bolts of heavy-colored silk, and two hundred bolts of plain silk as funeral gifts; coffin, shroud, silver and mercury for preservation, burial goods, and burial ground were all provided by the state; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Supporter-of-the-State Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the emperor mourned him deeply, sent officials to perform sacrifices, and granted five hundred taels of silver, ten bolts of fine silk, and two hundred bolts of plain silk; coffin, shroud, embalming materials, burial goods, and a grave site were all provided by the court; he was posthumously enfeoffed Supporter-of-the-State Grand General.

sentences.zh: 耶律余睹

translations.literal: Yelü Yudu
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Yudu

sentences.zh: 太祖已取臨潢府，賜詔余睹曰：「汝將兵在東路，前後戰未嘗不敗。

translations.literal: After Emperor Taizu had taken Linhuang Prefecture, he issued an edict to Yudu: "You command troops on the eastern route; in battle after battle you have never failed to be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu captured Linhuang, he sent Yudu an edict: "You command troops on the eastern front, and battle after battle you have lost.

sentences.zh: 今聞汝收合散亡，以拒我師。

translations.literal: Now I hear you are gathering scattered remnants to resist My army.
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear you are rallying scattered forces to resist my army.

sentences.zh: 朕已於今月十五日克上京，今將往取遼主矣。

translations.literal: I have on the fifteenth of this month taken the Upper Capital; now I am going to seize the Liao ruler.
translations.idiomatic: I took the Upper Capital on the fifteenth of this month and am now marching to capture the Liao emperor.

sentences.zh: 汝若治兵一決勝負，可指地期日相報。

translations.literal: If you wish to marshal troops and settle victory or defeat in one battle, you may designate a place and set a date to inform Me.
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to muster your forces and fight it out, name a place and a date and send word.

sentences.zh: 若知不敵，當率眾來降，無貽後悔。

translations.literal: If you know you cannot match Us, you should lead your multitude to surrender—do not bring regret upon yourself.
translations.idiomatic: If you know you cannot win, lead your men in surrender—do not invite regret.

sentences.zh: 」及太祖班師，闍母等還至遼河，方渡，余睹來襲，完顏背答、烏塔等殿，力戰卻之，獲甲馬五百匹。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizu withdrew his army, Chamu and others returned to the Liao River and were in mid-crossing when Yudu came to attack; Wanyan Beida, Wuta, and others formed the rearguard, fought fiercely, and drove him back, capturing five hundred sets of armor and horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu withdrew, Chamu's forces were crossing the Liao River when Yudu attacked; Wanyan Beida, Wuta, and others held the rear, fought him off, and captured five hundred sets of armor and horses.

sentences.zh: 天輔五年，余睹送款于咸州路都統，以所部來降，乞援接于桑林渡。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu, Yudu sent terms of surrender to the commander-in-chief of Xianzhou Circuit, came to submit with his following, and requested support to meet him at Sanglin Ford.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 5 (1121), Yudu sent surrender terms to the Xianzhou circuit commander, came in with his troops, and asked to be met at Sanglin Ford.

sentences.zh: 都統司以聞，詔曰：「余睹到日，使與其官屬偕來，餘眾處之便地。

translations.literal: The commander's office reported this; an edict said, "On the day Yudu arrives, have him come with his officials; settle the rest of his followers in a suitable place.
translations.idiomatic: The command reported upward; an edict ordered: "When Yudu arrives, have him come with his officers; settle the rest of his men wherever convenient.

sentences.zh: 」無何，余睹送上所受遼國宣誥，及器甲旗幟等，與將吏韓福奴、阿八、謝老、太師奴、蕭慶、醜和尚、高佛留、蒲答、謝家奴、五哥等來降。

translations.literal: Before long Yudu presented the Liao imperial patents and edicts he had received, along with weapons, armor, banners, and standards; he came to surrender with his officers Han Funu, Aba, Xie Lao, Taishinu, Xiao Qing, Chouheshang, Gao Foliu, Puda, Xiejianu, Wuge, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yudu presented the Liao patents and edicts he had held, along with arms, armor, and banners, and surrendered with officers including Han Funu, Aba, Xie Lao, Taishinu, Xiao Qing, Chouheshang, Gao Foliu, Puda, Xiejianu, and Wuge.

sentences.zh: 余睹作書，具言所以降之意，大概以謂：「遼主沉湎荒于遊畋，不恤政事，好佞人，遠忠直，淫刑吝賞，政煩賦重，民不聊生。

translations.literal: Yudu wrote a letter fully explaining his reasons for surrendering, stating in general: "The Liao ruler is sunk in dissipation and obsessed with hunting, heedless of government; he favors flatterers and keeps the loyal and upright at a distance; punishments are cruel and rewards stingy; government is burdensome and taxes heavy; the people cannot survive.
translations.idiomatic: Yudu wrote at length explaining why he surrendered, saying in essence: "The Liao emperor is sunk in pleasure and obsessed with the hunt, neglects government, favors flatterers and shuns the loyal, imposes cruel punishments and grudging rewards, and burdens the people with heavy taxes until they cannot live.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「樞密使得裏底本無材能，但阿諛取容，其子磨哥任以軍事。

translations.literal: He also wrote: "The Councilor-in-Chief Delidi has no talent whatsoever but flatters to win favor; his son Moge is entrusted with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Grand Councilor Delidi has no ability but flatters his way to favor; his son Moge has been put in charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「文妃長子晉王素系人望，宜為儲副，得裏底以元妃諸子己所自出，使晉王出繼文妃。

translations.literal: He also wrote: "The eldest son of Consort Wen, the Prince of Jin, has long enjoyed popular esteem and ought to be heir apparent; Delidi, because the sons of the Primary Consort were his own issue, had the Prince of Jin adopted out to Consort Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Consort Wen's eldest son, the Prince of Jin, has long enjoyed public esteem and should be heir apparent; Delidi, whose own sons were born to the Primary Consort, had the Prince of Jin adopted to Consort Wen instead.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「晉王與駙馬乙信謀複其樞密使，來告余睹共定大計，而所圖不成。

translations.literal: He also wrote: "The Prince of Jin and the imperial son-in-law Yixin plotted to restore his post as Councilor-in-Chief; they came to inform Yudu and together fixed a grand plan, but what they schemed did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "The Prince of Jin and the imperial son-in-law Yixin plotted to restore the prince's post as grand councilor; they confided in Yudu and laid a grand plan, but it came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「己粗更軍事，進策遼主，得裏底蔽之，遼主亦不省察。

translations.literal: He also wrote: "I myself had roughly reorganized military affairs and presented strategies to the Liao ruler, but Delidi concealed them, and the Liao ruler likewise did not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "I had reorganized military affairs and presented plans to the Liao emperor, but Delidi suppressed them and the emperor never looked into it.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「大金疆土日辟，余睹灼知天命，遂自去年春與耶律慎思等定議，約以今夏來降。

translations.literal: He also said: "The Great Jin's territory expands daily; Yudu clearly perceives Heaven's mandate; therefore from last spring he fixed plans with Yelü Shensi and others, agreeing to surrender this summer.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "The Jin realm grows daily; I clearly see where Heaven's mandate lies; from last spring I agreed with Yelü Shensi and others to surrender this summer.

sentences.zh: 近聞得裏底、高十捏等欲發，倉卒之際不及收合四遠，但率傍近部族戶三千、車五千兩、畜產數萬、遼北軍都統以兵追襲，遂棄輜重，轉戰至此。

translations.literal: Recently hearing that Delidi, Gao Shinie, and others were about to move, in the haste of the moment he could not gather forces from the four directions; he led only the nearby tribal households—three thousand families, five thousand carts, and tens of thousands of livestock; the commander-in-chief of the Northern Liao army pursued with troops; he abandoned baggage and fought his way here.
translations.idiomatic: When I heard Delidi and Gao Shinie were about to move against me, I had no time to rally distant tribes; I led only three thousand nearby households, five thousand carts, and tens of thousands of livestock; the northern Liao commander pursued me, and I abandoned my baggage fighting my way here.

sentences.zh: 所有官事職位姓名、人戶畜產之數，遣韓福奴具錄以聞。

translations.literal: The roster of official posts, names, households, and livestock is sent with Han Funu to report in full.
translations.idiomatic: Han Funu will submit a full roster of offices, names, households, and livestock.

sentences.zh: 」遂與其將吏來見，上撫慰之，遂賜坐，班同宰相，賜宴盡醉而罷。

translations.literal: He then came to an audience with his officers; the emperor comforted him, granted him a seat, ranked him equal to the chief councilors, and gave a banquet at which all drank their fill before dispersing.
translations.idiomatic: He then came to court with his officers; the emperor received him graciously, seated him in rank equal to the chief councilors, and held a banquet at which all drank their fill.

sentences.zh: 上命余睹以舊官領所部。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yudu to lead his following under his former title.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yudu to command his followers under his former title.

sentences.zh: 且諭之曰：「若能為國立功，別當獎用。

translations.literal: He further instructed him: "If you can render merit to the state, you will be separately rewarded and employed.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "If you render service to the state, you will be rewarded accordingly.

sentences.zh: 」自余睹降，益知遼人虛實矣。

translations.literal: From Yudu's surrender onward, they came to know ever more clearly the true condition of the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: After Yudu's surrender, the Jin learned far more about the Liao's real strength.

sentences.zh: 余睹在軍中屢乞侍妾及子，太祖疑之，詔咸州路都統司曰：「余睹家屬，善監護之。

translations.literal: While in the army Yudu repeatedly begged for concubines and a son; Emperor Taizu grew suspicious and issued an edict to the Xianzhou circuit command: "Yudu's family members—guard them well.
translations.idiomatic: In camp Yudu repeatedly asked for concubines and to see his son; Taizu grew suspicious and ordered the Xianzhou command: "Guard Yudu's family closely.

sentences.zh: 」複詔曰：「余睹降時，其民多強率而來者，恐在邊生變，宜徙之內地。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "When Yudu surrendered, many of his people were forcibly brought along; fearing unrest on the frontier, they should be relocated to the interior.
translations.idiomatic: A further edict said: "Many of Yudu's people were forcibly brought along when he surrendered; fearing unrest on the frontier, relocate them inland.

sentences.zh: 」都統杲取中京，余睹為鄉導，與希尹等招撫奚部。

translations.literal: Commander Gao took the Central Capital; Yudu served as guide and, with Xiyin and others, pacified and won over the Xi tribes.
translations.idiomatic: When Commander Gao took the Central Capital, Yudu guided the way and, with Xiyin and others, pacified the Xi tribes.

sentences.zh: 奉聖州降，其官吏皆遁去，余睹舉前監酒李師夔為節度使，進士沈璋為副使，州吏裴賾為觀察判官。

translations.literal: When Fengsheng Prefecture surrendered its officials all fled; Yudu recommended the former wine supervisor Li Shikui as military commissioner, jinshi degree-holder Shen Zhang as vice commissioner, and prefectural clerk Pei Ze as observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Fengsheng Prefecture surrendered, its officials fled; Yudu recommended former wine supervisor Li Shikui as military commissioner, jinshi Shen Zhang as vice commissioner, and clerk Pei Ze as observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 沈璋招集居民還業者三千餘，遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: Shen Zhang gathered more than three thousand residents who returned to their occupations; he was transferred to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhang brought back more than three thousand residents to their livelihoods and was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 久之，耶律麻者告余睹、吳十、劉剌結黨謀叛，及其未發宜先收捕。

translations.literal: After some time Yelü Mazhe reported that Yudu, Wu Shi, and Liu La had formed a faction to plot rebellion, and that they should be seized before they acted.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later Yelü Mazhe reported that Yudu, Wu Shi, and Liu La had formed a clique to rebel and should be arrested before they acted.

sentences.zh: 上召余睹等從容謂之曰：「今聞汝謀叛，誠然邪，其各無隱。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Yudu and the others and said calmly: "I now hear you plot rebellion—is it true? Each of you, hide nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Yudu and the others and said calmly: "I hear you plot rebellion—is it so? Speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 若果去，必須鞍馬甲胄器械之屬，當悉付汝，吾不食言。

translations.literal: If you truly wish to go, you will need saddles, horses, armor, weapons, and the like—I shall give them all to you; I do not break My word.
translations.idiomatic: If you truly mean to leave, you will need horses, armor, and weapons—I will give you everything; I do not break my word.

sentences.zh: 若再被擒，無祈免死。

translations.literal: If you are captured again, do not pray for exemption from death.
translations.idiomatic: If you are captured again, do not expect mercy.

sentences.zh: 欲留事我，則無懷異志，吾不汝疑。

translations.literal: If you wish to remain and serve Me, harbor no other designs—I will not suspect you.
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to stay and serve me, harbor no other designs—I will not doubt you.

sentences.zh: 」余睹等戰慄不能對，乃杖鐸剌七十，餘皆不問。

translations.literal: Yudu and the others trembled and could not reply; the emperor then had Duola beaten seventy strokes; the rest were not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Yudu and the others trembled and could not answer; the emperor had Duola beaten seventy strokes and questioned no one else.

sentences.zh: 天會三年，大舉伐宋，余睹為元帥右都監，宋兵四萬救太原，余睹、屋里海逆擊於汾河北，擒其帥郝仲連、張關索，統制馬忠，殺萬餘人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhui a great campaign was launched against the Song; Yudu served as right deputy commander-in-chief of the main army; forty thousand Song troops came to relieve Taiyuan; Yudu and Wulihai counterattacked north of the Fen River, capturing their commanders Hao Zhonglian and Zhang Guansuo, controller Ma Zhong, and killing more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 3 (1125) a major invasion of the Song was launched; Yudu served as right deputy commander-in-chief; forty thousand Song troops marched to relieve Taiyuan; Yudu and Wulihai counterattacked north of the Fen River, capturing commanders Hao Zhonglian and Zhang Guansuo and controller Ma Zhong, and killing more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 宗翰伐宋，余睹留西京。

translations.literal: When Zonghan attacked the Song, Yudu remained at the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Zonghan invaded the Song, Yudu stayed behind at the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 天會十年，余睹謀反，雲內節度使耶律奴哥等告之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianhui Yudu plotted rebellion; Yunnei military commissioner Yelü Nuge and others reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 10 (1132) Yudu plotted rebellion; Yunnei military commissioner Yelü Nuge and others informed on him.

sentences.zh: 余睹亡去，其黨燕京統軍蕭高六伏誅，蔚州節度使蕭特謀自殺。

translations.literal: Yudu fled; his accomplice, Yanjing commander-in-chief Xiao Gaoliu, was executed; Weizhou military commissioner Xiao Temou committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Yudu fled; his accomplice Yanjing commander Xiao Gaoliu was executed, and Weizhou military commissioner Xiao Temou killed himself.

sentences.zh: 邊部斬余睹及其諸子，函其首以獻。

translations.literal: Frontier units beheaded Yudu and his sons, boxed their heads, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier troops beheaded Yudu and his sons and sent their heads in tribute.

sentences.zh: 耶律奴哥加守太保兼侍中，趙公鑒、劉儒信、劉君輔等並授遙鎮節度使以賞之。

translations.literal: Yelü Nuge was promoted to Defender-in-Chief and concurrently Palace Attendant; Zhao Gongjian, Liu Ruxin, Liu Junfu, and others were all appointed distant military commissioners as reward.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Nuge was promoted to Defender-in-Chief and Palace Attendant; Zhao Gongjian, Liu Ruxin, Liu Junfu, and others were rewarded with appointments as distant military commissioners.

sentences.zh: 移剌窩斡，西北路契丹部族。

translations.literal: Yelü Wo Wo, of the Khitan tribal groups of the Northwestern Route.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Wo Wo, of the Khitan tribes of the Northwestern Route.

sentences.zh: 先從撒八為亂，受其偽署，後殺撒八，遂有其眾。

translations.literal: He first followed Saba in rebellion, accepted a false appointment from him, later killed Saba, and thus came to hold his following.
translations.idiomatic: He first followed Saba's rebellion and accepted a post in his regime, then killed Saba and took over his forces.

sentences.zh: 撒八者，初為招討司譯史。

translations.literal: Saba had originally been a translator-clerk in the Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Saba had originally served as a translator-clerk in the Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 正隆五年，海陵征諸道兵伐宋，使牌印燥合、楊葛盡征西北路契丹丁壯，契丹人曰：「西北路接近鄰國，世世征伐，相為仇怨。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenglong, Hailing conscripted troops from all circuits to attack the Song, sending Paoyin Zaohe and Yang Ge to conscript all able-bodied Khitan men of the Northwestern Route; the Khitan people said, "The Northwestern Route borders neighboring states; generation after generation we have fought wars and borne mutual enmity.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong 5 (1160) Hailing conscripted troops from every circuit for the Song campaign, sending Paoyin Zaohe and Yang Ge to draft every able Khitan man on the Northwestern Route; the Khitan protested: "The northwest borders enemy states; we have fought them generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 若男丁盡從軍，彼以兵來，則老弱必盡系累矣。

translations.literal: If all able-bodied men go to war and the enemy comes with troops, then the old, weak, women, and children will surely all be taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: If every fighting man is taken south, the enemy will march in and our women, children, and elderly will all be captured.

sentences.zh: 幸使者入朝言之。

translations.literal: We beg the envoy to enter court and report this.
translations.idiomatic: We beg that the envoy be sent to court to plead our case.

sentences.zh: 」燥合畏罪不敢言，楊葛深念後西北有事得罪，遂以憂死。

translations.literal: " Zaohe, fearing guilt, dared not speak; Yang Ge, brooding deeply that later if trouble arose in the northwest he would be held guilty, then died from worry.
translations.idiomatic: " Zaohe, fearing punishment, kept silent; Yang Ge, brooding that if trouble later broke out in the northwest he would be blamed, died of anxiety.

sentences.zh: 燥合複與牌印耶律娜、尚書省令史沒答涅合督起西北路兵。

translations.literal: Zaohe again, together with Paoyin Yelü Na and Secretariat clerk Modaniehe, supervised the mustering of Northwestern Route troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zaohe again, with Paoyin Yelü Na and Secretariat clerk Modaniehe, pressed the conscription of Northwestern Route troops.

sentences.zh: 契丹聞男丁當盡起，於是撒八、孛特補與部眾殺招討使完顏沃側及燥合，而執耶律娜、沒答涅合，取招討司貯甲三千，遂反。

translations.literal: When the Khitan heard that all able-bodied men were to be mobilized, thereupon Saba and Betebu with their following killed Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Woce and Zaohe, seized Yelü Na and Modaniehe, took three thousand sets of armor stored by the Pacification Commission, and then rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that every fighting man was to be drafted, Saba and Betebu led their followers to kill Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Woce and Zaohe, seize Yelü Na and Modaniehe, strip three thousand sets of armor from the Pacification Commission stores, and rise in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 議立豫王延禧子孫，眾推都監老和尚為招討使，山后四群牧、山前諸群牧皆應之。

translations.literal: They discussed installing a descendant of Prince Yu Yannian; the multitude acclaimed Superintendent Old Monk as pacification commissioner; the four horse pasturages behind the mountains and the various horse pasturages before the mountains all responded.
translations.idiomatic: They debated enthroning a descendant of Prince Yu Yannian; the rebels acclaimed Old Monk the Superintendent as pacification commissioner, and the pasture domains north and south of the mountains all joined.

sentences.zh: 迪斡群牧使徒單賽裏、耶魯瓦群牧使鶴壽等皆遇害，語在《鶴壽傳》中。

translations.literal: Dihua Pasturage Commissioner Tushan Saili, Yelüwa Pasturage Commissioner Hesou, and others were all murdered; the account is in the "Biography of Hesou."
translations.idiomatic: Dihua Pasturage Commissioner Tushan Saili, Yelüwa Pasturage Commissioner Hesou, and others were killed; their story is told in the "Biography of Hesou."

sentences.zh: 五院司部人老和尚那也亦殺節度使術甲兀者以應撒八。

translations.literal: A man of the Wuyuan Department, Old Monk Naye, also killed Military Commissioner Shujiawuzhe to respond to Saba.
translations.idiomatic: Old Monk Naye of the Wuyuan Department also killed Military Commissioner Shujiawuzhe to join Saba's revolt.

sentences.zh: 會甯八猛安牧馬於山后，至迪謀魯，賊盡奪其馬。

translations.literal: It happened that Ningba Company Commander was pasturing horses behind the mountains; when he reached Dimeru, the rebels seized all his horses.
translations.idiomatic: Ningba Company Commander was grazing horses in the northern hills; when he reached Dimeru, the rebels seized every mount.

sentences.zh: 辟沙河千戶十哥等與前招討使完顏麻潑殺烏古迪列招討使烏林答蒲盧虎，以所部趨西北路。

translations.literal: Company Commander Shige of Pishahe and others, together with former Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Mapo, killed Uguidilie Pacification Commissioner Ulinada Puluhu, and with their commands hurried toward the Northwestern Route.
translations.idiomatic: Company Commander Shige of Pishahe, together with former Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Mapo, killed Uguidilie Pacification Commissioner Ulinada Puluhu and marched their units toward the Northwestern Route.

sentences.zh: 室魯部節度使阿廝列追擊敗之，十哥與數騎遁去，合於撒八。

translations.literal: Shilu Department Military Commissioner Asilie pursued, defeated them; Shige with several horsemen fled and joined Saba.
translations.idiomatic: Shilu Department Military Commissioner Asilie pursued and routed them; Shige escaped with a few riders and rejoined Saba.

sentences.zh: 咸平府謀克括裏，與所部自山后逃歸，咸平少尹完顏餘裏野欲收捕括裏家屬，括裏與其党招誘富家奴隸，數日得眾二千，遂攻陷韓州及柳河縣，遂趨咸平。

translations.literal: Company Commander Kuoli of Xianping Prefecture, with his command fleeing back from behind the mountains, when Xianping Vice Magistrate Wanyan Yuliye wished to arrest Kuoli's family members, Kuoli with his partisans recruited wealthy households' slaves; within days he gathered two thousand followers, then captured Han Prefecture and Liuhe County, then pressed toward Xianping.
translations.idiomatic: Company Commander Kuoli of Xianping Prefecture fled back from the north with his command; when Vice Magistrate Wanyan Yuliye tried to seize Kuoli's family, Kuoli and his faction recruited slaves from wealthy households and within days rallied two thousand men, captured Han Prefecture and Liuhe County, and marched on Xianping.

sentences.zh: 餘裏野發兵迎擊之，兵敗，賊遂據咸平，於是繕完器甲，出府庫財物以募兵，賊勢益張。

translations.literal: Yuliye dispatched troops to meet and attack them, was defeated; the rebels then occupied Xianping, whereupon they repaired armor and weapons, distributed treasury wealth to recruit troops, and the rebels' power grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Yuliye marched out to meet them and was defeated; the rebels seized Xianping, refitted arms and armor, spent treasury funds to recruit troops, and their strength swelled.

sentences.zh: 權曹家山猛安綽質，集兵千餘，扼幹夜河，賊不得東。

translations.literal: Acting Caojiashan Company Commander Chuezhi gathered more than a thousand troops, blocked Ganye River, and the rebels could not advance east.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Caojiashan Company Commander Chuezhi mustered over a thousand men and held the Ganye River, blocking the rebels' eastward advance.

sentences.zh: 綽質兵敗，括裏遂犯濟州。

translations.literal: Chuezhi's troops were defeated; Kuoli then invaded Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chuezhi was defeated, and Kuoli invaded Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會宿直將軍孛術魯吳括剌徵兵于速頻路，遇括裏於信州，與猛安烏延查剌兵二千，擊敗括裏。

translations.literal: It happened that Palace Duty General Bieshulu Wukuala was conscripting troops on the Supin Route; he encountered Kuoli at Xin Prefecture and, with Company Commander Wuyan Zhala's two thousand troops, defeated Kuoli.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Duty General Bieshulu Wukuala was raising troops on the Supin Route when he met Kuoli at Xin Prefecture; with two thousand men under Company Commander Wuyan Zhala he routed Kuoli.

sentences.zh: 括裏收余眾趨東京，是時世宗為東京留守，以兵四百人拒之。

translations.literal: Kuoli gathered his remaining forces and pressed toward the Eastern Capital; at that time Emperor Shizong was resident commissioner of the Eastern Capital and resisted with four hundred troops.
translations.idiomatic: Kuoli regrouped and marched on the Eastern Capital; Emperor Shizong, then resident commissioner there, met him with four hundred troops.

sentences.zh: 賊至常安縣，聞空中擊鼓聲如數千鼓者，候見旌旗蔽野，傳言留守以十萬兵至矣，即引還，亦以其眾合於撒八。

translations.literal: When the rebels reached Chang'an County, they heard drumming in the air as though from thousands of drums; on reconnaissance they saw banners covering the plain; rumor had it that the resident commissioner had arrived with a hundred thousand troops; they thereupon withdrew, and also merged their following with Saba.
translations.idiomatic: At Chang'an County the rebels heard thunderous drumming as of a thousand drums, saw banners blanketing the fields, and heard that the resident commissioner was coming with a hundred thousand men; they retreated and rejoined Saba.

sentences.zh: 海陵使樞密使僕散忽土、西京留守蕭懷忠將兵一萬，與右衛將軍蕭禿剌討平之。

translations.literal: Hailing sent Privy Councilor Pusan Hutu and Western Capital Resident Commissioner Xiao Huaizhong to lead ten thousand troops, together with Right Guard General Xiao Tuci, to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing dispatched Privy Councilor Pusan Hutu and Western Capital Resident Commissioner Xiao Huaizhong with ten thousand troops, along with Right Guard General Xiao Tuci, to put down the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 禿剌與之相持數日，連與戰皆無功，而糧餉不繼，禿剌退歸臨潢。

translations.literal: Tuci confronted them for several days; repeated battles all achieved nothing, and supplies failed; Tuci withdrew to Linhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Tuci faced them for days but won no battle; supplies ran short, and he withdrew to Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 禿剌雖不能克敵，而撒八自度大軍必相繼而至，勢不可支，謀歸於大石，乃率眾沿龍駒河西出。

translations.literal: Although Tuci could not defeat the enemy, Saba judged that great armies would surely follow in succession and that the situation could not be sustained; he planned to submit to Da Shi and led his multitude west along the Longju River to exit.
translations.idiomatic: Though Tuci failed to crush them, Saba judged that Jin armies would keep coming and his position was untenable; he planned to join Da Shi and led his forces west along the Longju River.

sentences.zh: 及僕散忽土、蕭懷忠等兵至，與禿剌合兵追至河上，不及而還。

translations.literal: When Pusan Hutu, Xiao Huaizhong, and the others' troops arrived and joined Tuci in pursuit to the river, they failed to overtake them and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Pusan Hutu and Xiao Huaizhong arrived and combined with Tuci to pursue to the river, they failed to catch Saba and turned back.

sentences.zh: 忽土、懷忠、禿剌坐逗遛不即追賊，皆誅死。

translations.literal: Hutu, Huaizhong, and Tuci were punished for dawdling and not immediately pursuing the rebels; all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Hutu, Huaizhong, and Tuci were executed for dragging their feet and failing to pursue the rebels immediately.

sentences.zh: 北京留守蕭賾不能制其下，殺降人而取其婦女，亦坐誅。

translations.literal: Northern Capital Resident Commissioner Xiao Ze could not control his subordinates; they killed surrendered men and took their women; he too was punished with execution.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Capital Resident Commissioner Xiao Ze lost control of his men, who slaughtered captives and seized their women; he too was executed.

sentences.zh: 於是，白彥恭為北面兵馬都統，紇石烈志寧副之，守顏彀英為西北面兵馬都統，西北路招討使唐括孛姑的副之，以討撒八等。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bai Yangong was made Northern Route military commander-in-chief, with Heshenlie Zhining as deputy; Shouyan Gouying was made Northwestern Route military commander-in-chief, with Northwestern Route Pacification Commissioner Tangguo Begede as deputy, to attack Saba and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Yangong was appointed Northern Route commander-in-chief with Heshenlie Zhining as his deputy; Shouyan Gouying became Northwestern Route commander-in-chief with Northwestern Route Pacification Commissioner Tangguo Begede as deputy, to campaign against Saba.

sentences.zh: 撒八既西行，而舊居山前者皆不欲往，偽署六院節度使移刺窩斡、兵官陳家殺撒八，執老和尚、孛特補等。

translations.literal: Saba having already gone west, those who had formerly lived before the mountains all did not wish to go; the falsely appointed Six Circuits Military Commissioner Yelü Wo Wo and Military Officer Chen Jia killed Saba and seized Old Monk, Betebu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Once Saba marched west, his followers from south of the mountains refused to follow; the rebel Six Circuits Military Commissioner Yelü Wo Wo and Military Officer Chen Jia killed Saba and seized Old Monk, Betebu, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 至是，窩斡始自為都元帥，陳家為都監，擁眾東還，至臨潢府東南新羅寨。

translations.literal: At this point Wo Wo for the first time made himself commander-in-chief, with Chen Jia as superintendent; he led his following eastward back to Xinlou Stockade southeast of Linhuang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo now declared himself commander-in-chief, with Chen Jia as superintendent, and led his forces east to Xinlou Stockade southeast of Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 世宗使移剌紮八、前押軍謀克播斡、前牌印麻駭、利涉軍節度判官馬腦等招之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong sent Yelü Zhaba, former Escort Company Commander Bowo, former Paoyin Mahai, and Lishe Army Military Commissioner Adjunct Ma Nao and others to summon them to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong sent Yelü Zhaba, former Escort Company Commander Bowo, former Paoyin Mahai, and Lishe Army adjutant Ma Nao to offer them surrender terms.

sentences.zh: 紮八等見窩斡，以上意諭之。

translations.literal: Zhaba and the others met Wo Wo and conveyed the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaba and his party met Wo Wo and delivered the emperor's message.

sentences.zh: 窩斡已約降，已而複謂紮八曰：「若降，爾能保我輩無事乎？

translations.literal: Wo Wo had already agreed to surrender, but then again said to Zhaba, "If we surrender, can you guarantee that we will come to no harm?
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo had agreed to surrender, then asked Zhaba: "If we submit, can you guarantee our safety?

sentences.zh: 」紮八曰：「我知招降耳，其他豈能必哉。」

translations.literal: " Zhaba said, "I know only how to summon surrender; as for the rest, how can I be certain?"
translations.idiomatic: " Zhaba replied, "I can only bring you terms of surrender—beyond that I cannot promise anything."

sentences.zh: 紮八見窩斡兵眾強，車帳滿野，意其可以有成，因說之曰：「我之始來，以汝輩不能有為，今觀兵勢強盛如此，汝等欲如群羊為人所驅去乎，將欲待天時乎？

translations.literal: Zhaba saw that Wo Wo's troops were strong and wagons and tents filled the plain; he thought they might succeed, and therefore urged him, saying, "When I first came, I thought you could accomplish nothing; now seeing military power flourishing thus, do you wish to be like a flock of sheep driven off by others, or do you wish to await Heaven's timing?
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Wo Wo's vast encampment, Zhaba changed his mind and urged him on: "When I arrived I thought you had no chance—but with strength like this, will you be driven like sheep, or wait for Heaven's moment?

sentences.zh: 若果有大志，吾亦不復還矣。

translations.literal: If you truly have great ambition, I shall not return either.
translations.idiomatic: If you truly mean to fight, I will not go back.

sentences.zh: 」賊將有前孛特本部族節度使逐斡者，言：「昔谷神丞相，賢能人也，嘗說他日西北部族當有事。

translations.literal: " Among the rebel generals was former Betebu Tribal Military Commissioner Zhuwo, who said, "In former times Chancellor Gushen, a worthy man, once said that someday the northwestern tribes would have trouble.
translations.idiomatic: " Rebel general Zhuwo, former Betebu Tribal Military Commissioner, said: "Chancellor Gushen once prophesied that the northwestern tribes would rise one day.

sentences.zh: 今日正合此語，恐不可降也。

translations.literal: Today this saying fits exactly; I fear we cannot surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Today proves him right—we cannot surrender.

sentences.zh: 」於是，窩斡遂決意不復肯降矣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Wo Wo firmly resolved no longer to be willing to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo then firmly refused to surrender.

sentences.zh: 紮八亦留賊中，惟麻駭、播斡還歸。

translations.literal: Zhaba also remained among the rebels; only Mahai and Bowo returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaba stayed with the rebels; only Mahai and Bowo returned.

sentences.zh: 窩斡乃引兵攻臨潢府，總管移室懣出城戰，兵少被執，賊遂圍臨潢，眾至五萬。

translations.literal: Wo Wo then led troops to attack Linhuang Prefecture; Supervisor Yishi Men went out to battle; his troops were few and he was captured; the rebels then besieged Linhuang, reaching fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo marched on Linhuang; Supervisor Yishi Men sallied out with too few men, was captured, and the rebels besieged the city with fifty thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 正隆六年十二月己亥，窩斡遂稱帝，改元天正。

translations.literal: On the jihai day of the twelfth month of the sixth year of Zhenglong, Wo Wo thereupon declared himself emperor and changed the era name to Tianzheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day of the twelfth month of Zhenglong 6 (1161), Wo Wo declared himself emperor under the era name Tianzheng.

sentences.zh: 是時，北面都統白彥敬、副統紇石烈志寧在北京，聞世宗即位，以兵來歸。

translations.literal: At this time Northern Route commander-in-chief Bai Yanjing and deputy commander Heshenlie Zhining were at the Northern Capital; hearing of Emperor Shizong's accession, they came with troops to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Route commander Bai Yanjing and his deputy Heshenlie Zhining were at the Northern Capital; on hearing of Emperor Shizong's accession they marched south to submit.

sentences.zh: 世宗使元帥左都監吾紮忽、同知北京留守事完顏骨只救臨潢，晝夜兼行，比至臨潢，賊已解圍去攻泰州。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong sent Left Army Supervisor Wuzhahu and Associate Northern Capital Resident Commissioner Wanyan Guzhi to relieve Linhuang; day and night they pressed on; by the time they reached Linhuang, the rebels had already lifted the siege and gone to attack Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong sent Left Army Supervisor Wuzhahu and Associate Northern Capital Resident Commissioner Wanyan Guzhi to relieve Linhuang; they marched day and night, but the rebels had already broken off the siege and moved on Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 吾紮忽追及於窊曆，兩軍已陣將戰，押軍猛安契丹忽剌叔以所部兵應賊，吾紮忽軍遂敗。

translations.literal: Wuzhahu overtook them at Wali; both armies had formed ranks about to battle; Escort Company Commander Khitan Hulashu with his command's troops responded to the rebels; Wuzhahu's army was then defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhahu caught them at Wali as both sides deployed for battle; Escort Company Commander Hulashu the Khitan went over to the rebels with his unit, and Wuzhahu was routed.

sentences.zh: 泰州節度使烏裏雅率千餘騎與窩斡遇，烏裏雅兵複敗，僅以數騎脫歸。

translations.literal: Taizhou Military Commissioner Wuliya led more than a thousand horsemen and encountered Wo Wo; Wuliya's troops were again defeated; he escaped back with only several horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhou Military Commissioner Wuliya met Wo Wo with over a thousand cavalry, was routed again, and escaped with only a handful of riders.

sentences.zh: 賊勢愈振，城中震駭，莫敢出戰。

translations.literal: The rebels' momentum grew ever stronger; the city was shaken with terror; none dared go out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels' momentum swelled; terror gripped the city and no one dared sally out.

sentences.zh: 賊四面登城，押軍猛安烏古孫阿裏補率軍士數人，各持刀以身率先循城擊賊力戰，斫刈甚眾，賊乃退走，城賴以完。

translations.literal: The rebels climbed the walls on all four sides; Escort Company Commander Wugusun Alibu led several soldiers, each wielding a blade and taking the lead in person along the wall to strike the rebels and fight fiercely; they cut down many; the rebels then retreated; the city was preserved thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels scaled the walls on every side; Escort Company Commander Wugusun Alibu led a handful of soldiers sword in hand along the ramparts and cut down many rebels until they withdrew; the city held.

sentences.zh: 泰州司吏顏盞蒲查奏捷，除忠翊校尉，賜銀五十兩、重彩十端。

translations.literal: Taizhou clerk Yanzhan Pucha reported the victory; he was appointed Loyal Assistant Commander, granted fifty taels of silver and ten bolts of heavy brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhou clerk Yanzhan Pucha reported the victory and was made Loyal Assistant Commander, rewarded with fifty taels of silver and ten bolts of brocade.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，右副元帥完顏謀衍率諸軍北征窩斡。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief Wanyan Moyan led the various armies north to campaign against Wo Wo.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 2, Right Deputy Commander Wanyan Moyan led the armies north against Wo Wo.

sentences.zh: 二月壬戌詔曰：「應諸人若能於契丹賊中自拔歸者，更不問元初首從及被威脅之由，奴婢、良人罪無輕重並行免放。

translations.literal: On the renxu day of the second month an edict said, "All persons who can extricate themselves from among the Khitan rebels and return shall no longer be questioned as to whether they were original ringleaders or coerced; slaves and commoners, regardless of the severity of guilt, shall all be pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day of the second month an edict declared: "Anyone who breaks away from the Khitan rebels and returns shall not be questioned about past leadership or coercion; slaves and commoners alike, whatever their offense, shall be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 曾有官職及糾率人眾來歸者，仍與官賞，依本品量材敘使。

translations.literal: Those who formerly held office and those who rallied people to come and submit shall still receive official rewards; according to their original rank and measured by ability they shall be appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Former officials and those who bring followers home shall still receive rank and reward, appointed according to their prior rank and merit.

sentences.zh: 其同來人各從所願處收系，有才能者亦與錄用。

translations.literal: Their companions who come together shall each be enrolled wherever they wish; those with talent shall also be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Their companions may settle wherever they choose; the capable shall also be enlisted.

sentences.zh: 內外官員郎君群牧直撒百姓人家驅奴、宮籍監人等，並放為良，亦從所願處收系，與免三年差役。

translations.literal: Inner and outer officials, langjun, pasture guards, zhi sa commoners, household bondsmen, palace registry overseers, and others shall all be released as commoners; they too may be enrolled wherever they wish and shall be granted exemption from corvée for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Officials, langjun, pasture guards, zhi sa commoners, household slaves, palace registry overseers, and the like shall all be freed; they too may settle where they wish and be exempt from corvée for three years.

sentences.zh: 或能捕殺首領而歸者，准上施行，仍驗勞績約量遷賞。

translations.literal: Those who can capture or kill rebel leaders and return shall be treated according to the above provisions and, examining merit, be promoted and rewarded in due measure.
translations.idiomatic: Those who capture or kill rebel leaders shall receive the rewards above, with promotion scaled to their merit.

sentences.zh: 如捕獲窩斡者，猛安加三品官授節度使，謀克加四品官授防禦使，庶人加五品官授刺史。

translations.literal: If Wo Wo is captured, a company commander shall be raised three ranks and made military commissioner, a platoon commander raised four ranks and made defense commissioner, a commoner raised five ranks and made prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever captures Wo Wo shall receive: company commanders promoted three ranks to military commissioner, platoon commanders four ranks to defense commissioner, commoners five ranks to prefect.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「尚書省，如節度防禦使捉獲窩斡者與世襲猛安，刺史捉獲者與世襲謀克，驅奴、宮籍監人亦與庶人同。

translations.literal: " An edict said, "To the Secretariat: if a military or defense commissioner captures Wo Wo, grant a hereditary company command; if a prefect captures him, grant a hereditary platoon command; bondsmen and palace registry overseers shall be treated the same as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: " A further edict to the Secretariat: "Military or defense commissioners who capture Wo Wo receive hereditary company commands; prefects receive hereditary platoon commands; bondsmen and palace overseers are treated as commoners.

sentences.zh: 」複詔宰臣，遍諭將士，能捕殺窩斡者加特進、授真總管。

translations.literal: " Again the chief ministers were edicted to proclaim throughout to officers and soldiers that whoever can capture or kill Wo Wo shall receive the special advancement rank and be appointed true commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: " The chief ministers were further instructed to tell every soldier that whoever captures or kills Wo Wo shall be made Grand Mentor and appointed full commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 於是，括裏將犯韓州，聞元帥兵至，不戰遁去，將轉趨懿、宜州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Kuoli was about to invade Han Prefecture; hearing that the commander's army had arrived, he fled without fighting and was about to turn toward Yi and Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kuoli was marching on Han Prefecture when he heard the imperial army was coming; he fled without a fight and turned toward Yi and Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 謀衍屯懿州慶雲縣，及屯川州武平縣，奏請糧運當遣人護送，兵仗乞選精良者付之。

translations.literal: Moyan encamped at Qingyun County, Yi Prefecture, and at Wuping County, Chuan Prefecture; he memorialized requesting that grain transport be escorted and that fine weapons be selected and entrusted to the escorts.
translations.idiomatic: Moyan encamped at Qingyun in Yi Prefecture and Wuping in Chuan Prefecture, requesting escorts for supply convoys and the best arms for them.

sentences.zh: 詔以南征逃還軍士就往屯戍，如不足，量于富家簽調，就近地簽步軍，給仗護送糧運。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that soldiers who had fled back from the southern campaign be sent immediately to garrison duty; if insufficient, draft proportionally from wealthy households, draft infantry nearby, and provide weapons to escort grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered soldiers returned from the southern campaign reassigned to garrison duty; if more were needed, conscript from wealthy households and local infantry to escort the supply trains.

sentences.zh: 詔平章政事移剌元宜往泰州規措邊事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Grand Counselor Yelü Yuanyi to go to Taizhou to manage frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Counselor Yelü Yuanyi was ordered to Taizhou to manage frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 前安遠大將軍斡裏嫋、猛安七斤、庶人阿裏葛、磨哥等自窩斡中來降，斡裏嫋、七斤加昭武大將軍，阿裏葛武義將軍，磨哥忠勇校尉。

translations.literal: Former Anyuan General Woli Niao, Company Commander Qijin, commoner Alige, Moge, and others came to surrender from among Wo Wo's forces; Woli Niao and Qijin were promoted to General of Manifest Martiality; Alige to General of Martial Righteousness; Moge to Loyal Valor Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Former Anyuan General Woli Niao, Company Commander Qijin, and commoners Alige and Moge defected from Wo Wo's camp; Woli Niao and Qijin were made Generals of Manifest Martiality, Alige General of Martial Righteousness, and Moge Loyal Valor Commander.

sentences.zh: 窩斡遂自泰州往攻濟州，欲邀糧運。

translations.literal: Wo Wo then from Taizhou went to attack Ji Prefecture, intending to intercept grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo marched from Taizhou to attack Ji Prefecture, aiming to intercept the supply convoys.

sentences.zh: 元帥完顏謀衍與右監軍完顏福壽、左都監吾紮忽合兵，甲士萬三千人，曷懶路總管徒單克甯、廣甯尹僕散渾坦、同知廣甯尹完顏岩雅、肇州防禦使唐括烏也為左翼，臨海節度使紇石烈志寧、曷速館節度使神土懣、同知北京留守完顏骨只、淄州刺史尼龐古鈔兀為右翼，至術虎崖，盡委輜重，士卒齎數日糧，輕騎襲之。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Wanyan Moyan combined forces with Right Army Supervisor Wanyan Fushou and Left Army Supervisor Wuzhahu, thirteen thousand armored troops; Helan Route Supervisor Tushan Kening, Guangning Prefect Pusan Hundan, Associate Guangning Prefect Wanyan Yanya, and Zhaozhou Defense Commissioner Tangguo Wuye as the left wing; Linhai Military Commissioner Heshenlie Zhining, Esuguan Military Commissioner Sheng Tumu, Associate Northern Capital Resident Commissioner Wanyan Guzhi, and Zizhou Prefect Nipanggu Chaowu as the right wing; they reached Shuhuya, left all baggage behind, soldiers carrying several days' rations, light cavalry raiding them.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Wanyan Moyan joined Right Army Supervisor Wanyan Fushou and Left Army Supervisor Wuzhahu with thirteen thousand armored troops; the left wing under Helan Route Supervisor Tushan Kening, Guangning Prefect Pusan Hundan, Associate Guangning Prefect Wanyan Yanya, and Zhaozhou Defense Commissioner Tangguo Wuye, and the right wing under Linhai Military Commissioner Heshenlie Zhining, Esuguan Military Commissioner Sheng Tumu, Associate Northern Capital Resident Commissioner Wanyan Guzhi, and Zizhou Prefect Nipanggu Chaowu, reached Shuhuya, abandoned all baggage, and with several days' rations carried by the troops struck with light cavalry.

sentences.zh: 糺椀群牧人契丹颭者，與其弟孛迭、挼剌，皆棄家自賊中來降。

translations.literal: Jiuwan Pasturage Khitan Zhanzhe, with his younger brothers Bedie and Roula, all abandoned their families and came to surrender from among the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhe the Khitan of Jiuwan Pasturage, with his brothers Bedie and Roula, deserted their families and defected from the rebels.

sentences.zh: 糺者謂謀衍曰：「賊中馬肥健，官軍馬疲弱，此去賊八十里，比遇賊馬已憊。

translations.literal: Zhanzhe said to Moyan, "The rebels' horses are fat and strong; the government army's horses are weak and spent; from here to the rebels is eighty li; by the time we meet them their horses will already be weary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhe told Moyan: "The rebels' horses are fresh and strong, ours are tired; they are eighty li away—by the time we meet them their mounts will be spent.

sentences.zh: 賊輜重去此不遠，我攻之，賊必救其巢穴，賊至馬必疲，我馬少得息，所謂攻其所必救，以逸待勞者也。

translations.literal: The rebels' baggage is not far from here; if we attack it, the rebels will surely rescue their nest; when they arrive their horses will be weary and our horses will get a little rest—what is called attacking where they must rescue, awaiting the weary with the rested.
translations.idiomatic: Their baggage train is close; strike it and they must come to its defense—they will arrive exhausted while ours rest. That is the classic 'attack what they must save' and meet strength with rest.

sentences.zh: 」謀衍從之，乘夜亟發，會大風路暗不能辨，遲明行三十里許，與賊輜重相近，整兵少憩。

translations.literal: " Moyan followed this advice, setting out urgently by night; they encountered strong wind and dark roads and could not distinguish their way; at dawn they had marched about thirty li, were close to the rebels' baggage, formed ranks and rested briefly.
translations.idiomatic: Moyan agreed and marched by night; a gale blew and the road was dark; at dawn, after thirty li, they were near the rebel baggage and halted to regroup.

sentences.zh: 窩斡趨濟州，知大軍取其輜重，乃還救，遇於長濼。

translations.literal: Wo Wo was pressing toward Ji Prefecture; learning that the great army was taking his baggage, he then turned back to rescue; they met at Changpo.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo was racing toward Ji Prefecture when he learned the Jin army had seized his baggage; he turned back to rescue it and met the Jin forces at Changpo.

sentences.zh: 既陣，謀衍別設伏於左翼之側，賊四百餘騎突出左翼伏兵之間，徒單克寧射卻之。

translations.literal: Once ranks were formed, Moyan separately set an ambush on the flank of the left wing; more than four hundred rebel horsemen burst out between the left-wing ambush; Tushan Kening shot them back.
translations.idiomatic: As the armies deployed, Moyan hid troops on the left flank; four hundred rebel riders burst through the ambush line, and Tushan Kening drove them back with arrows.

sentences.zh: 是日，別部諸將與賊對者，勝負未分，相去五里許而立。

translations.literal: That day, generals of separate divisions facing the rebels had not yet decided victory or defeat; they stood about five li apart.
translations.idiomatic: That day other detachments faced the rebels without a clear outcome, standing some five li apart.

sentences.zh: 左翼萬戶襄別與賊戰，賊陣動，襄麾軍乘之，突出其後，俱與大軍不相及。

translations.literal: Left-wing Ten-thousand Household Commander Xiangbie fought the rebels; the rebel formation stirred; Xiang waved his army to press the advantage, burst out behind them, and both became cut off from the main army.
translations.idiomatic: Left-wing commander Xiangbie engaged the rebels; when their line wavered he pressed the attack, swung behind them, and was cut off from the main force.

sentences.zh: 襄以善射者二十騎，率眾自賊後擊之，賊不能支，乘勢麾軍擊其一偏，賊遂卻。

translations.literal: Xiang with twenty skilled archers on horseback led the multitude to strike from behind the rebels; the rebels could not hold; seizing the momentum he waved his army to strike one flank; the rebels then retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang took twenty crack archers and attacked from the rear; the rebels buckled; he pressed one flank and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 襄遂與大軍合，而別部諸將皆至，整陣力戰，忽反風揚砂石，賊陣亂，官軍馳擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Xiang then rejoined the main army; the generals of separate divisions all arrived; they formed ranks and fought hard; suddenly a reverse wind raised sand and stones; the rebel formation was thrown into disorder; the government army charged and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang rejoined the main army; all detachments converged and fought hard; a sudden headwind whipped up sand and gravel; the rebel line broke; the imperial army charged and smashed them.

sentences.zh: 追北十餘裏，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Pursuing the fleeing enemy for more than ten li, they beheaded and captured a great multitude.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit ran more than ten li, with heavy casualties and captures.

sentences.zh: 詔以糺者為武義將軍，孛迭昭信校尉，挼剌忠翊校尉。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Zhanzhe General of Martial Righteousness, Bedie Trustworthy Commander, and Roula Loyal Assistant Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhe was made General of Martial Righteousness, Bedie Trustworthy Commander, and Roula Loyal Assistant Commander.

sentences.zh: 糺除同知建州事，未之官，卒。

translations.literal: Zhan was appointed Associate Jianzhou Administrator but never took office and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was appointed Associate Administrator of Jianzhou but died before taking office.

sentences.zh: 孛迭取家賊中，遂被害，上憫之，後以挼剌為汝州都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Bedie went to fetch his family from among the rebels and was thereupon killed; the emperor pitied him; later Roula was made Youzhou Chief Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Bedie went back into rebel territory to fetch his family and was killed; the emperor mourned him and later made Roula Chief Inspector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 窩斡率其眾西走，謀衍追及之於霿𩃭河。

translations.literal: Wo Wo led his multitude fleeing west; Moyan overtook him at the Menglong River.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo fled west; Moyan caught up with him at the Menglong River.

sentences.zh: 賊已濟，毀其津口，紇石烈志寧軍先至，不克渡，乃對岸為疑兵，以夾穀清臣、徒單海羅兩萬戶於下流渡河，值支港兩岸鬥絕且濘淖，命軍士束柳填港而過。

translations.literal: The rebels had already crossed and destroyed the ford; Heshenlie Zhining's army arrived first and could not cross; he then set up a feint on the opposite bank and had Ten-thousand Household Commanders Jiagu Qingchen and Tushan Hailuo cross downstream; they encountered branch channels with steep banks on both sides and mud; he ordered soldiers to bundle willows to fill the channels and pass.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had already crossed and destroyed the ford; Heshenlie Zhining's vanguard could not follow; he feinted from the opposite bank while Ten-thousand Household Commanders Jiagu Qingchen and Tushan Hailuo forded downstream; where side channels ran steep and miry, he ordered willow bundles packed into the mud to bridge a crossing.

sentences.zh: 追之數裏，得平地，方食，賊眾奄至。

translations.literal: Pursuing several li, they reached flat ground and were just eating when rebel forces suddenly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Several li into the pursuit they reached open ground and were at meals when rebels appeared without warning.

sentences.zh: 志寧軍急整陣，賊自南岡馳下，沖陣者三，志寧力戰，流矢中左臂，戰自若。

translations.literal: Zhining's army hurriedly formed ranks; the rebels charged down from the southern ridge; they charged the formation three times; Zhining fought hard; a stray arrow struck his left arm; he fought as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining's troops scrambled into formation as rebels swept down from the southern ridge and charged three times; an arrow struck Zhining's left arm, but he fought on without faltering.

sentences.zh: 大軍畢至，左翼騎兵先與賊接，賊據上風縱火，乘煙擊官軍，官軍步兵亦至，並力合戰，凡十余合，軍士苦風煙皆植立如癡。

translations.literal: The main army all arrived; left-wing cavalry first engaged the rebels; the rebels held the upwind position and set fires, attacking the government army through the smoke; government infantry also arrived; together they joined battle; altogether more than ten clashes; soldiers suffering from wind and smoke all stood planted like idiots.
translations.idiomatic: The main army arrived; left-wing cavalry engaged first as the rebels, holding the upwind, set fires and struck through the smoke; infantry joined and both sides fought through more than ten clashes; choked by wind and smoke, soldiers stood dazed as if stunned.

sentences.zh: 會天降雨，風止，官軍奮擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: Just then Heaven sent rain; the wind stopped; the government army fought fiercely and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell, the wind died, and the imperial army struck hard and routed them.

sentences.zh: 徒單克寧追奔十五里，賊前厄溪澗不得亟渡，多殺傷。

translations.literal: Tushan Kening pursued the fleeing enemy fifteen li; the rebels were blocked ahead by streams and ravines and could not quickly cross; many were killed and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Tushan Kening pursued fifteen li; rebels bottlenecked at streams and ravines suffered heavy losses.

sentences.zh: 賊既渡，官軍亦渡，少憩，賊反旆來攻，克甯以大軍不繼，令軍士皆下馬射賊。

translations.literal: Once the rebels had crossed, the government army also crossed and rested briefly; the rebels turned their banners and came to attack; Kening because the main army had not followed ordered soldiers all to dismount and shoot the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: After both sides crossed, the rebels wheeled about and attacked; with the main army not yet up, Kening ordered his men to dismount and shoot.

sentences.zh: 賊引卻而南，克寧亦將引而北，士未及騎馬，賊複來衝突，官軍少卻，回渡澗北。

translations.literal: The rebels withdrew toward the south; Kening was also about to withdraw toward the north; the soldiers had not yet remounted when the rebels again came charging; the government army retreated slightly and recrossed to the north of the stream.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pulled back south; Kening began to withdraw north, but before his men could remount the rebels charged again; the imperial troops fell back across the stream.

sentences.zh: 大軍至，賊遂引去。

translations.literal: When the main army arrived, the rebels thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army arrived, the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 四月，詔元帥府曰；

translations.literal: In the fourth month, an edict to the Marshal's Headquarters said:
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month an edict was sent to the Marshal's Headquarters:

sentences.zh: 「應契丹賊人，與大兵未戰已前投降者，不得殺傷，仍加安撫。

translations.literal: "All Khitan rebels who surrender before engaging the main army shall not be harmed and shall receive reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: "Khitan rebels who surrender before battle shall not be harmed and shall be reassured.

sentences.zh: 敗走以後，招誘來降者，除奴婢准已虜為定外，親屬分付圓聚。

translations.literal: Those persuaded to come and submit after defeat and flight, aside from bondsmen counted according to those already captured, shall have their kin gathered and reunited.
translations.idiomatic: Those who surrender after defeat, aside from bondsmen already taken captive, shall have their kin gathered and reunited.

sentences.zh: 仍官為換贖。」

translations.literal: The government shall also redeem them."
translations.idiomatic: The state shall also redeem them."

sentences.zh: 窩斡既敗，謀衍不復追討，駐軍白濼。

translations.literal: Wo Wo having been defeated, Moyan no longer pursued; he encamped at Baipo.
translations.idiomatic: After Wo Wo's defeat, Moyan stopped pursuing and encamped at Baipo.

sentences.zh: 窩斡攻懿州不克，遂殘破川州，將遁於山西，而北京亦不邀擊之。

translations.literal: Wo Wo attacked Yi Prefecture without success, then ravaged Chuan Prefecture and was about to flee into Shanxi, yet the Northern Capital also did not intercept him.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo failed to take Yi Prefecture, ravaged Chuan Prefecture, and prepared to flee west into the hills, yet the Northern Capital force did not intercept him.

sentences.zh: 於是，發驍騎軍二千、曷懶路留屯京師軍三千，號稱二萬，會寧濟州軍六千亦號二萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon two thousand Elite Cavalry troops and three thousand Helan Route garrison troops left at the capital were dispatched, claiming twenty thousand; six thousand Huining and Ji Prefecture troops also claimed twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand Elite Cavalry and three thousand Helan Route garrison troops from the capital were dispatched under the banner of twenty thousand; six thousand from Huining and Ji Prefecture were likewise counted as twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 元帥左都監高忠建總兵，沃州刺史烏古論蒲查為曷懶路押軍萬戶，祁州刺史烏林答剌撒為濟州押軍萬戶，右驍騎副都指揮使烏延查剌為驍騎萬戶，祁州刺史宗甯為會甯路押軍萬戶，右宣徽使宗亨為北京路都統，吏部郎中完顏達吉為副統，會元帥府討擊之。

translations.literal: Left Army Supervisor Gao Zhongjian commanded the army; Wozhou Prefect Wugulun Pucha served as Helan Route Escort Ten-thousand Household Commander; Qizhou Prefect Ulinada Lasa served as Ji Prefecture Escort Ten-thousand Household Commander; Right Elite Cavalry Deputy Commander Wuyan Zhala served as Elite Cavalry Ten-thousand Household Commander; Qizhou Prefect Zongning served as Huining Route Escort Ten-thousand Household Commander; Right Palace Commissioner Zongheng served as Northern Capital Route commander-in-chief; Ministry of Personnel Director Wanyan Daji served as deputy commander; they joined the Marshal's Headquarters to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Left Army Supervisor Gao Zhongjian took overall command; Wozhou Prefect Wugulun Pucha became Helan Route escort commander, Qizhou Prefect Ulinada Lasa Ji Prefecture escort commander, Right Elite Cavalry Deputy Commander Wuyan Zhala Elite Cavalry commander, Qizhou Prefect Zongning Huining Route escort commander, Right Palace Commissioner Zongheng Northern Capital Route commander-in-chief, and Ministry of Personnel Director Wanyan Daji his deputy; together they joined the Marshal's Headquarters to hunt the rebels down.

sentences.zh: 詔使尚廄局副使蒲察蒲盧渾往懿州戒敕將帥，上曰：「朕委卿等討賊，乃聞不就賊趨戰，而駐兵閑緩，經涉累月，雖曾追襲，乃不由有水草之地，以致馬疲弱不能百里而還。

translations.literal: An edict envoy, Deputy Stable Commissioner Pucha Puluhun, was sent to Yi Prefecture to admonish the generals; the emperor said, "I entrusted you to suppress the rebels, yet I hear you did not press toward battle but encamped at leisure; months passed; though you once pursued, you did not take routes with water and grass, so that the horses grew weak and could not go a hundred li before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Stable Commissioner Pucha Puluhun was sent to Yi Prefecture to rebuke the generals; the emperor said: "I charged you to suppress the rebels, yet you linger in camp instead of closing with the enemy; though you pursued once, you avoided watered pasture and your horses grew too weak to chase a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 後雖破賊，而縱諸軍劫掠，數日後方追北霿𩃭河，亦不乘勝，輒複引還。
