translations.literal: Later, though you defeated the rebels, you let the armies plunder; only days afterward did you pursue north to the Menglong River, and even then you did not press the victory but again withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Even after you broke them, you allowed looting and waited days before pursuing to the Menglong River—and then failed to press the advantage and withdrew again.

sentences.zh: 賊遂入涉近地，北京、懿州由此受兵。

translations.literal: The rebels then entered nearby territory; the Northern Capital and Yi Prefecture thereby suffered attack.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then raided the frontier; Beijing and Yi Prefecture bore the brunt.

sentences.zh: 朕欲重譴汝等，以方任兵事，且圖後功。

translations.literal: I wish to punish you severely, but since you are still entrusted with military affairs, I look to your future achievements.
translations.idiomatic: I would punish you severely, but with the campaign still in your hands I am giving you one more chance.

sentences.zh: 當盡心一力，毋得似前怠弛。

translations.literal: You must devote yourselves wholeheartedly and must not be slack as before.
translations.idiomatic: Devote yourselves fully and do not repeat such negligence.

sentences.zh: 」上謂蒲盧渾曰：「卿若聞賊在近，即當監督討伐。

translations.literal: " The emperor said to Puluhun, "If you hear the rebels are nearby, you must at once supervise the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: " He told Puluhun: "If you hear the rebels are near, supervise the attack at once.

sentences.zh: 用命力戰者疏記以聞，朕將約量遷賞。

translations.literal: Record in memorial those who obey orders and fight hard; I shall promote and reward them according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: Report those who fight with all their strength; I shall reward them according to merit."

sentences.zh: 無或承徇上官，抑有功、濫署無功者。

translations.literal: Let none currying favor with superiors suppress the meritorious or appoint without merit those without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Do not curry favor with superiors, suppress the deserving, or promote the undeserving.

sentences.zh: 善戢士卒、勿縱虜掠。

translations.literal: Well restrain the soldiers; do not allow plundering.
translations.idiomatic: Keep your troops under discipline and do not permit looting.

sentences.zh: 」以紇石烈志甯為元帥右監軍，右副元帥完顏謀衍、元帥右監軍完顏福壽召還京師，咸平路總管完顏兀帶復舊職。

translations.literal: " Heshenlie Zhining was made Right Army Supervisor of the Marshal's Headquarters; Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief Wanyan Moyan and Right Army Supervisor Wanyan Fushou were recalled to the capital; Xianping Route Supervisor Wanyan Udai was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: " Heshenlie Zhining was appointed Right Army Supervisor; Right Deputy Commander Wanyan Moyan and Right Army Supervisor Wanyan Fushou were recalled to the capital, and Xianping Route Supervisor Wanyan Udai returned to his former post.

sentences.zh: 謀衍男斜哥在軍中多暴橫，詔押歸本管。

translations.literal: Moyan's son Xiege was excessively violent and overbearing in the army; an edict ordered him escorted back to his home jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Moyan's son Xiege had been bullying the troops; he was ordered escorted back to his home command.

sentences.zh: 窩斡使所親招節度使移裏堇窟域，窟域執其使送官，與窩斡連戰有功，遷宣武將軍，賜銀五百兩、衣二襲。

translations.literal: Wo Wo sent a close associate to win over Military Commissioner Yiliqin Kuyu; Kuyu seized the envoy and sent him to the authorities; having fought Wo Wo repeatedly with merit, he was promoted to General of Manifest Martiality and granted five hundred taels of silver and two suits of clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo sent an agent to win over Military Commissioner Yiliqin Kuyu; Kuyu arrested the envoy and turned him in; for repeated victories against Wo Wo he was promoted to General of Manifest Martiality and given five hundred taels of silver and two suits of clothing.

sentences.zh: 起運在中都弓萬五千、箭一百五十萬赴懿州。

translations.literal: Transport was raised from the Central Capital of fifteen thousand bows and one million five hundred thousand arrows to Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen thousand bows and one and a half million arrows were shipped from the Central Capital to Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 平章政事移剌元宜、甯昌軍節度使宗敘入見，詔使自中道卻還軍中，宣諭元宜、謀衍注意經略邊事。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Yili Yuanxuan and Ningchang Army Military Commissioner Zongxu came for audience; an edict had them turn back midway and return to the army, instructing Yuanxuan and Moyan to give attention to border strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Yili Yuanxuan and Ningchang Army Military Commissioner Zongxu were summoned to court, then ordered to turn back mid-journey and return to their commands, with instructions that Yuanxuan and Moyan must give priority to border strategy.

sentences.zh: 師久無功，尚書右丞僕散忠義願效死力除邊患，世宗嘉歎。

translations.literal: The army had campaigned long without success; Vice Director of the Right of the Ministry of Works Pusan Zhongyi volunteered to exert himself unto death to eliminate the border threat; Emperor Shizong praised and sighed with admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign had dragged on without success; Vice Director Pusan Zhongyi offered to give his life to end the border crisis; Emperor Shizong praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 六月，忠義拜平章政事兼右副元帥，宗敘為兵部尚書，各賜弓矢、具鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Zhongyi was appointed Grand Councilor and concurrent Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief; Zongxu was made Minister of War; each was granted bow and arrows and a fully saddled and bridled horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Zhongyi was made Grand Councilor and Right Deputy Commander, Zongxu Minister of War; each received bow and arrows and a saddled war horse.

sentences.zh: 出內府金銀十萬兩佐軍用。

translations.literal: One hundred thousand taels of gold and silver from the inner treasury were disbursed to assist military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred thousand taels of gold and silver from the palace treasury were allocated for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「軍中將士有犯，除連職奏聞，餘依軍法約量決責，有功者依格遷賞。

translations.literal: An edict said: "When officers and soldiers in the army commit offenses, except those implicating their entire chain of command who must be reported upward, the rest shall be judged and punished according to military law as appropriate; those with merit shall be promoted and rewarded according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Offenses among the rank and file shall be punished under military law at the commander's discretion, except cases implicating an entire chain of command, which must be reported to the throne; the meritorious shall be promoted according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 」以大名尹宗尹為河南路統軍使，河南路統軍都監蒲察世傑為西北路副統，賜弓矢佩刀廄馬，從忠義征行。

translations.literal: " Daming Prefect Zongyin was made Henan Route Commander-in-Chief; Henan Route Army Supervisor Pucha Shijie was made Northwestern Route Deputy Commander; bow and arrows, belt sword, and stable horse were granted; they followed Zhongyi on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: " Daming Prefect Zongyin was appointed Henan Route commander, Army Supervisor Pucha Shijie Northwestern Route deputy commander; each received bow and arrows, sword, and remount, and joined Zhongyi's campaign.

sentences.zh: 詔諭諸軍將士曰：「兵久駐邊陲，蠹費財用無成功，百姓不得休息。

translations.literal: An edict instructed the officers and soldiers of the armies, saying: "The troops have long encamped on the frontier, wasting resources without success, and the people cannot rest.
translations.idiomatic: An edict to the armies read: "Your long encampment on the frontier has drained the treasury without victory, and the people know no peace.

sentences.zh: 今命平章政事僕散忠義兼右副元帥，同心戮力以底戡定。

translations.literal: Now Grand Councilor Pusan Zhongyi is appointed concurrent Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief; with one heart and united strength to achieve pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Pusan Zhongyi is now Right Deputy Commander; unite in full force to bring this rebellion to an end.

sentences.zh: 右副元帥謀衍罷為同判大宗正事。」

translations.literal: Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief Moyan was dismissed and made Associate Minister of the Imperial Clan Office."
translations.idiomatic: Right Deputy Commander Moyan is relieved and appointed Associate Minister of the Imperial Clan Office."

sentences.zh: 詔居庸關、古北口譏察契丹奸細，捕獲者加官賞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered scrutiny at Juyong Pass and Gubeikou for Khitan spies; those captured would receive promotion and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Posts at Juyong Pass and Gubeikou were ordered to watch for Khitan spies; captors would receive promotion and reward.

sentences.zh: 萬戶溫蒂罕阿魯帶以兵四千屯古北口，薊州、石門關等處各以五百人守之。

translations.literal: Ten-thousand Household Commander Wendihan Aludai encamped at Gubeikou with four thousand troops; Jizhou, Shimen Pass, and other places were each garrisoned with five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Wendihan Aludai took four thousand men to Gubeikou; Jizhou, Shimen Pass, and other posts received five hundred men each.

sentences.zh: 海陵末年，阿魯帶為猛安，移剌娜為牌印祗候，起契丹部族兵被執，至是挺身來降。

translations.literal: In the last years of Hailing, Aludai was a meng'an and Yili Na a paoyin attendant; Khitan tribal troops were conscripted and seized; at this time they came forward in person to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In Hailing's final years Aludai had been a meng'an and Yili Na a paoyin attendant; when Khitan tribal levies were seized for conscription, both now came forward to surrender.

sentences.zh: 世宗以阿魯帶為濟州押軍萬戶，移剌娜為同知濼州事。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong made Aludai Escort Ten-thousand Household Commander of Ji Prefecture and Yili Na Associate Prefect of Woluo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong appointed Aludai Ji Prefecture escort commander and Yili Na associate prefect of Woluo.

sentences.zh: 西南路招討使完顏思敬為都統，賜金牌一、銀牌二，西北路招討使唐括孛古底副之。

translations.literal: Southwestern Route Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Sijing was made commander-in-chief, granted one gold tablet and two silver tablets; Northwestern Route Pacification Commissioner Tangguo Begede served as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Southwestern Route Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Sijing was made overall commander with one gold and two silver tablets; Northwestern Route Pacification Commissioner Tangguo Begede served as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 以兵五千往會燕子城舊戍軍，視地形沖要或於狗濼屯駐，遠斥候，賊至即戰，不以晝夜為限。

translations.literal: With five thousand troops he was to join the old garrison army at Swallow City; judging crucial terrain he might encamp at Goupo; distant scouts were to be posted; when rebels came, fight at once, without limit of day or night.
translations.idiomatic: He was to join the old garrison at Swallow City with five thousand men, encamp at any strategic point such as Goupo, post distant scouts, and engage the enemy whenever they appeared, day or night.

sentences.zh: 詔思敬曰：「契丹賊敗必走山后，可選新馬三千，加芻纇以備追襲。」

translations.literal: An edict to Sijing said: "When the Khitan rebels are defeated they will surely flee behind the mountains; select three thousand fresh horses and supply fodder to prepare for pursuit."
translations.idiomatic: Sijing was instructed: "Defeated Khitan rebels will flee north into the hills; ready three thousand fresh horses with fodder for the pursuit."

sentences.zh: 僕散忠義至軍中。

translations.literal: Pusan Zhongyi arrived at the army.
translations.idiomatic: Pusan Zhongyi reached the front.

sentences.zh: 是時，窩斡西走花道，眾尚八萬。

translations.literal: At this time Wo Wo fled west along Huadao; his followers still numbered eighty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo was fleeing west along Huadao with some eighty thousand men still in his train.

sentences.zh: 忠義、高忠建軍與賊遇，萬戶查剌、蒲查為左翼，宗亨統之；

translations.literal: Zhongyi and Gao Zhongjian's army encountered the rebels; Ten-thousand Household Commanders Zhala and Pucha formed the left wing, commanded by Zongheng;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi and Gao Zhongjian's forces met the rebels; Commanders Zhala and Pucha formed the left wing under Zongheng;

sentences.zh: 宗寧、剌撒為右翼，宗敘統之；

translations.literal: Zongning and Lasa formed the right wing, commanded by Zongxu;
translations.idiomatic: Zongning and Lasa the right wing under Zongxu;

sentences.zh: 世傑亦在左翼中，與賊夾河為陣。

translations.literal: Shijie was also in the left wing; they drew up battle lines facing the rebels across a river.
translations.idiomatic: Shijie fought in the left wing; the two sides faced each other across a river.

sentences.zh: 賊渡河，以兵四萬餘先犯左翼軍，查剌以六百騎奮擊敗之。

translations.literal: The rebels crossed the river; with more than forty thousand troops they first struck the left wing; Zhala with six hundred cavalry charged fiercely and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels forded the river and hit the left wing first with forty thousand men; Zhala charged with six hundred horsemen and broke them.

sentences.zh: 複以四萬眾與左翼軍戰，宗亨、世傑七謀克指畫失宜，陣亂敗於賊。

translations.literal: Again with forty thousand they fought the left wing; Zongheng and Shijie's seven company commanders directed poorly; the formation fell into disorder and was defeated by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: They returned with forty thousand and assailed the left wing again; Zongheng and Shijie's seven company commanders bungled their deployment, the line collapsed, and the rebels prevailed.

sentences.zh: 世傑挺身投于查剌軍中，賊圍查剌軍，查剌力戰，宗敘以右翼軍來救，賊乃去。

translations.literal: Shijie threw himself bodily into Zhala's force; the rebels surrounded Zhala's army; Zhala fought hard; Zongxu with the right wing came to the rescue, and the rebels then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shijie plunged into Zhala's ranks; the rebels surrounded Zhala's contingent; Zhala fought on until Zongxu brought the right wing to the rescue and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「自契丹作逆，有為賊詿誤者，不問如何從賊，但能複業，與免本罪。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Since the Khitan rebelled, those misled by the rebels—regardless of how they followed the rebels—if they can return to their occupations, their original crimes shall be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Since the Khitan rebellion began, all who were led astray—whatever their past offense—shall be pardoned if they return to honest livelihood.

sentences.zh: 如能率眾來附，或能殺捕首領而降，或執送賊所扇誘作亂之人，皆與量加官爵。

translations.literal: If they can lead their followers to submit, or kill and capture leaders and surrender, or seize and deliver those whom the rebels incited to riot, all shall receive commensurate promotion of rank and title.
translations.idiomatic: Those who bring followers to submit, capture rebel leaders, or deliver the agitators shall receive rank and honors according to their deeds.

sentences.zh: 朕念正隆南征，猛安亡者招還被戮，已命其子孫襲其職。

translations.literal: I reflect that in the Zhenglong southern campaign, meng'an who fled and were summoned back were executed; I have already ordered their descendants to inherit their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Recall that in Hailing's southern campaign, fugitive meng'an who returned were put to death—I have already ordered their heirs restored to office.

sentences.zh: 爾等勿懲前事，故懷遲疑。

translations.literal: Do not take warning from those earlier events and therefore harbor hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Do not let past examples make you hesitate.

sentences.zh: 賊軍今既破散，山后諸處皆命將士遏其逃路，爾等雖欲不降終將安往？

translations.literal: The rebel army is now broken and scattered; behind the mountains at every place officers and soldiers have been ordered to block their escape routes; even if you wish not to surrender, where in the end can you go?
translations.idiomatic: The rebel host is shattered, and troops throughout the northern hills block every escape route—if you will not surrender, where can you go?

sentences.zh: 若猶疑貳，俱就焚滅，悔及矣。」

translations.literal: If you still doubt and waver, all will be destroyed together; regret will come too late."
translations.idiomatic: Persist in doubt and you will all be destroyed—and then it will be too late for regret."

sentences.zh: 窩斡自花道西走，僕散忠義、紇石烈志甯以大軍追及於嫋嶺西陷泉。

translations.literal: Wo Wo fled west from Huadao; Pusan Zhongyi and Heshenlie Zhining with the great army overtook him at Xianquan west of Niaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo fled west from Huadao; Pusan Zhongyi and Heshenlie Zhining overtook him with the main army at Xianquan, west of Niaoling.

sentences.zh: 明日，賊軍三萬騎涉水而東。

translations.literal: The next day the rebel army, thirty thousand horsemen, waded across the water heading east.
translations.idiomatic: The next day thirty thousand rebel horsemen forded the stream heading east.

sentences.zh: 大軍先據南岡，左翼軍自岡為陣，迤邐而北，步軍繼之，右翼軍繼步軍北引而東，作偃月陣，步軍居中，騎兵據其兩端，使賊不見首尾。

translations.literal: The great army first seized the southern ridge; the left wing formed ranks from the ridge, winding northward; infantry followed; the right wing followed the infantry north and then east, forming a crescent formation; infantry at the center, cavalry holding both ends, so the rebels could not see head or tail.
translations.idiomatic: The main force seized the southern ridge first; the left wing lined the ridge northward, infantry behind, the right wing trailing north then east in a crescent—the infantry in the center, cavalry at both horns, hiding the army's full extent from the enemy.

sentences.zh: 是日，大霧晦冥，既陣霧開，少頃晴霽，賊見左翼據南岡不敢擊，擊右翼軍，烏延查剌力戰，賊稍卻。

translations.literal: That day thick fog darkened the sky; once the formation was set the fog lifted; shortly after the sky cleared; the rebels, seeing the left wing holding the southern ridge, did not dare attack; they attacked the right wing; Wuyan Zhala fought hard and the rebels fell back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: That day a dense fog shrouded the field; when the lines were set the fog lifted and sunshine followed; seeing the left wing hold the ridge, the rebels attacked the right instead; Wuyan Zhala fought hard and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 志甯與夾穀清臣、烏林答剌撒、鐸剌合戰，賊大敗，將涉水去，泥濘不得亟渡。

translations.literal: Zhining together with Jiagu Qingchen, Ulinada Lasa, and Dola fought; the rebels were utterly defeated; about to cross the water and flee, the mud and mire would not let them cross quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining, Jiagu Qingchen, Ulinada Lasa, and Dola pressed the attack; the rebels broke utterly; as they tried to ford the stream, mud trapped them on the bank.

sentences.zh: 大軍逐北，人馬相蹂踐而死，不可勝數，陷泉皆平，餘眾蹈籍而過，或奔潰竄匿林莽間。

translations.literal: The great army pursued north; men and horses trampled one another to death beyond counting; Xianquan was levelled; the remainder passed by treading over the fallen; some fled in rout and hid in scrub and thickets.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin army pressed the pursuit; men and horses trampled one another to death beyond count until Xianquan was level with the corpses; survivors scrambled over the dead or fled into the brush.

sentences.zh: 大軍踵擊之，俘斬萬計，生擒其弟偽六院司大王嫋。

translations.literal: The great army followed in pursuit; captures and kills numbered in the tens of thousands; his younger brother, the falsely appointed Six Circuits Commissioner Prince Niao, was taken alive.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit continued; tens of thousands were killed or captured, including Wo Wo's brother, the rebel Six Circuits Commissioner Prince Niao.

sentences.zh: 窩斡僅與數騎脫去，鈔兀、清臣追四十餘裏不及，斬千餘級，獲車帳甚眾。

translations.literal: Wo Wo escaped with only several horsemen; Chaowu and Qingchen pursued more than forty li without overtaking him; more than a thousand heads were cut; wagons and tents captured were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo escaped with a handful of riders; Chaowu and Qingchen chased forty li without catching him, cutting down over a thousand and seizing vast stores of wagons and tents.

sentences.zh: 其母徐輦舉營自落括岡西走，志寧追之，盡獲輜重，俘五萬餘人，雜畜不可勝計。

translations.literal: His mother Xulian raised camp and fled west from Luoguo Ridge; Zhining pursued; all baggage was captured; more than fifty thousand were taken prisoner; mixed livestock were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo's mother Xulian broke camp west of Luoguo Ridge; Zhining pursued, seizing all her baggage, taking fifty thousand prisoners, and livestock beyond count.

sentences.zh: 偽節度使六及其部族皆降。

translations.literal: The falsely appointed Military Commissioner Liu and his tribal followers all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Military Commissioner Liu and his followers all submitted.

sentences.zh: 詔北京副統完顏達吉括本部馬，規辦芻糧，仍使達吉為監戰官，錄有功者聞奏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Northern Capital Deputy Commander Wanyan Daji to muster horses of his own command, arrange fodder and grain, and additionally made Daji battle overseer, recording the meritorious and reporting upward.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Capital Deputy Commander Wanyan Daji was ordered to round up his own command's horses and gather fodder; he was made battle overseer and instructed to report all meritorious service.

sentences.zh: 詔選中都、西京兩路新舊軍萬人備守禦，以窩斡敗走，恐或衝突也。

translations.literal: An edict selected ten thousand men from new and old armies of the Central Capital and Western Capital routes to stand ready for defense, because Wo Wo, defeated and fleeing, might raid.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand troops from the Central and Western Capital circuits were mobilized for defense, lest the fleeing Wo Wo strike at vulnerable points.

sentences.zh: 僕散忠義使使奏捷，詔略曰：「平章政事右副元帥忠義使使來奏大捷。

translations.literal: Pusan Zhongyi sent envoys to report victory; the edict in summary said: "Grand Councilor and Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief Zhongyi's envoys came to report a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Pusan Zhongyi's envoys reported a great victory; the edict in part read: "Grand Councilor and Right Deputy Commander Zhongyi's messengers report a decisive victory.

sentences.zh: 或被軍俘獲，或自能來服，或無所歸而投拜，或將全屬歸附，或分領家族來降，或嘗受偽命，及自來曾與官軍鬥敵，皆釋其罪。

translations.literal: Whether captured by the army, coming to submit of their own accord, having nowhere to turn and kneeling in submission, bringing entire followings to submit, leading families separately to surrender, or having once received false appointments and having personally fought against the official army—all shall have their crimes released.
translations.idiomatic: Whether taken in battle, coming of their own will, having nowhere else to turn, bringing whole followings or families to submit, or even if they had held rebel office and fought the imperial army—all crimes are forgiven.

sentences.zh: 其散亡人內，除窩斡一身，不以大小官員是何名色，卻來歸附者，亦准釋放。

translations.literal: Among the scattered and fugitive, except Wo Wo himself, regardless of what rank or title, great or small, those who return to submit shall likewise be released.
translations.idiomatic: Among the scattered fugitives, all who return to submit—regardless of rank or title—shall be pardoned, save Wo Wo alone.

sentences.zh: 有能誅捕窩斡，或於不從招納亡去人內誅捕以來，及或能率眾于掌軍官及隨處官司投降者，並給官賞。

translations.literal: Those who can kill or capture Wo Wo, or among those who fled refusing surrender can kill or capture and bring them in, or who can lead their followers to surrender to army commanders or local officials—all shall be granted rank and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever kills or captures Wo Wo, or brings in fugitives who refused surrender, or leads followers to submit to any army post or local office shall receive rank and reward.

sentences.zh: 各路撫納來者，毋得輒加侵損。

translations.literal: Each route in pacifying and receiving those who come must not rashly add injury or harm.
translations.idiomatic: Every circuit receiving surrendering rebels must not molest them.

sentences.zh: 無資給者，不以是何路分，隨有糧處安置，仍官為養濟。」

translations.literal: Those without provisions, regardless of which route jurisdiction, shall be settled wherever grain is available, and the government shall provide sustenance."
translations.idiomatic: Those without means shall be settled wherever food is available, regardless of jurisdiction, and supported at public expense."

sentences.zh: 窩斡收合散卒萬餘人，遂入奚部，以諸奚自益，時時出兵寇速魯古澱、古北口、興化之間。

translations.literal: Wo Wo gathered scattered soldiers numbering more than ten thousand, then entered Xi territory, augmenting himself with various Xi tribes, from time to time sending troops to raid between Surug Lake, Gubeikou, and Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo regrouped over ten thousand scattered troops and entered Xi territory, recruiting Xi bands to his strength and raiding between Surug Lake, Gubeikou, and Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 溫蒂罕阿魯帶守古北口，與戰敗焉。

translations.literal: Wendihan Aludai defended Gubeikou and was defeated in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wendihan Aludai, defending Gubeikou, was defeated.

sentences.zh: 詔完顏謀衍、蒲察烏裏雅、蒲察蒲盧渾以兵三千，合舊屯兵五千，擊之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wanyan Moyan, Pucha Wuliya, and Pucha Puluhun with three thousand troops, joining five thousand old garrison troops, to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Moyan, Pucha Wuliya, and Pucha Puluhun were ordered to attack with three thousand men, joined to five thousand garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 詔守顏思敬以所部兵入奚地，會大軍討窩斡。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wanyan Sijing to enter Xi territory with his own troops and join the great army in suppressing Wo Wo.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Sijing was ordered to take his command into Xi territory and join the main army against Wo Wo.

sentences.zh: 賊黨霿𩃭河猛安蒲速越遣人至帥府約降，詔令擒捕窩斡，許以官賞。

translations.literal: The rebel partisan Menglong River Meng'an Pususan Zhongyi sent men to the marshal's headquarters to arrange surrender; an edict ordered the capture of Wo Wo, promising rank and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Menglong River meng'an Pususan Zhongyi, a rebel partisan, sent envoys to the marshal's headquarters offering to surrender on condition that Wo Wo be captured; rank and reward were promised.

sentences.zh: 賊將降者甚眾。

translations.literal: Rebel generals surrendering were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Many rebel officers surrendered.

sentences.zh: 其散走者聞詔書招降，亦多降者。

translations.literal: Those scattered and fleeing, hearing the edict summoning surrender, also largely surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Scattered fugitives who heard the surrender edict also came in in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 其餘多疾疫而死，無複鬥志。

translations.literal: The remainder mostly died of pestilence and had no will to fight again.
translations.idiomatic: The rest died mostly of plague and lost all will to fight.

sentences.zh: 窩斡自度勢窮，乃謀自羊城道西京奔夏國，大軍追之益急，其眾複多亡去，度不得西，乃北走沙陀間。

translations.literal: Wo Wo, judging his position hopeless, then planned to flee west along Yangcheng Road through the Western Capital to Xi Xia; the great army pursued ever more urgently; his followers again largely deserted; judging he could not go west, he then fled north among the Shatuo.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his cause hopeless, Wo Wo planned to flee west through the Western Capital toward Xi Xia; pursued ever more closely, his followers deserted again; unable to go west, he turned north into Shatuo country.

sentences.zh: 詔尚書省：「凡脅從之家被俘掠遂致離散，宜從改正。

translations.literal: An edict to the Secretariat: "All households of the coerced who were captured and plundered and thereby scattered should be rectified according to policy.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat was instructed: "Families of the coerced who were captured and separated must be restored according to policy.

sentences.zh: 將士往往藏匿其人，有司檢括分付。」

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers often hid such persons; the authorities were to investigate and assign them back."
translations.idiomatic: Officers who hide such people must be searched out and the victims returned to their families."

sentences.zh: 監軍志寧獲賊稍合住，釋而弗殺，縱還賊中，使誘其親近捕窩斡以自效，許以官賞。

translations.literal: Army Supervisor Zhining captured the rebel Shahezhu, released him without killing, and sent him back among the rebels, having him induce his close associates to capture Wo Wo to redeem himself, promising rank and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor Zhining captured the rebel Shahezhu, spared his life, and sent him back to the enemy camp to persuade his kinsmen to capture Wo Wo in exchange for rank and reward.

sentences.zh: 九月庚子，稍合住與神獨斡執窩斡，詣右都臨完顏思敬降，並獲其母徐輦及其妻、子、子婦、弟、侄，盡收偽金銀牌印。

translations.literal: On the gengzi day of the ninth month, Shahezhu together with Shenduwo seized Wo Wo and came to Right Army Supervisor Wanyan Sijing to surrender; they also captured his mother Xulian and his wife, sons, daughters-in-law, younger brother, and nephews; all false gold and silver tablets and seals were taken.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day of the ninth month Shahezhu and Shenduwo seized Wo Wo and surrendered to Right Army Supervisor Wanyan Sijing, together with his mother Xulian, wife, sons, daughters-in-law, brother, and nephews; all rebel gold and silver seals were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 唐括孛古底獲前胡裏改節度使什溫及其家屬。

translations.literal: Tangguo Begede captured former Huligai Military Commissioner Shiwen and his family.
translations.idiomatic: Tangguo Begede captured former Huligai Military Commissioner Shiwen and his family.

sentences.zh: 西北路招討使李家奴獲偽樞密使逐斡等三十餘人，複與猛安泥本婆果追偽監軍那也至天成縣，那也乃降，乃獲偽都元帥醜哥及金牌一、銀牌五。

translations.literal: Northwestern Route Pacification Commissioner Lijianu captured the falsely appointed Privy Councillor Zhuwo and more than thirty others; again with Meng'an Niben Boguo he pursued the falsely appointed Army Supervisor Naye to Tiancheng County; Naye then surrendered; thereupon the falsely appointed Commander-in-Chief Chouge was captured along with one gold tablet and five silver tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Northwestern Route Pacification Commissioner Lijianu captured the rebel Privy Councillor Zhuwo and thirty others; with meng'an Niben Boguo he chased rebel Army Supervisor Naye to Tiancheng County, where Naye surrendered and rebel Commander-in-Chief Chouge was taken along with one gold and five silver tablets.

sentences.zh: 志甯與清臣、宗甯、速哥等追餘黨至燕子城，盡得其黨。

translations.literal: Zhining with Qingchen, Zongning, Suge, and others pursued the remaining partisans to Swallow City and captured all their band.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining, Qingchen, Zongning, and Suge pursued the remaining rebels to Swallow City and rounded up the entire band.

sentences.zh: 前至抹拔裏達之地，悉獲之，逆党遂平。

translations.literal: Advancing to Mobalida territory, all were captured; the rebel faction was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on to Mobalida and captured them all; the rebellion was fully suppressed.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，皇太子率百官上表賀。

translations.literal: On the jiachen day, the crown prince led the hundred officials in submitting a congratulatory memorial.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the crown prince led the court in a congratulatory memorial.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，詔天下。

translations.literal: On the yisi day, an edict was issued to the empire.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi an edict went out to the realm.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，完顏思敬獻俘于京師，窩斡梟首於市，磔其手足，分懸諸京府。

translations.literal: On the xinhai day, Wanyan Sijing presented captives at the capital; Wo Wo's head was displayed in the marketplace; his limbs were dismembered and hung separately at various capitals and prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Wanyan Sijing presented the captives at the capital; Wo Wo's head was displayed in the marketplace, his limbs dismembered and hung in the major cities.

sentences.zh: 其母徐輦及妻子皆戮之。

translations.literal: His mother Xulian and wife and children were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Xulian, wife, and children were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 契丹降人皆拘其器仗，貧不能自給者官為養濟。

translations.literal: Khitan who surrendered were all required to surrender their weapons; those too poor to support themselves were sustained by the government.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendering Khitan were disarmed; those too poor to live on their own were maintained at public expense.

sentences.zh: 括裏、紮八率眾南走，詔左宣徽使宗亨追及之。

translations.literal: Kuoli and Zhaba led their followers south in flight; an edict ordered Left Palace Commissioner Zongheng to overtake them.
translations.idiomatic: Kuoli and Zhaba fled south with their followers; Left Palace Commissioner Zongheng was ordered to overtake them.

sentences.zh: 紮八詐稱降，宗亨信其言，遂不與戰。

translations.literal: Zhaba falsely claimed surrender; Zongheng believed his words and therefore did not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaba feigned surrender; Zongheng believed him and withheld his attack.

sentences.zh: 紮八紿之曰：「括裏驚走，願追之。

translations.literal: Zhaba deceived him, saying: "Kuoli fled in panic; I wish to pursue him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaba deceived him: "Kuoli fled in panic—I wish to pursue him.

sentences.zh: 」宗亨縱紮八去。

translations.literal: " Zongheng let Zhaba go.
translations.idiomatic: " Zongheng released Zhaba.

sentences.zh: 益都猛安欲以所部追括裏、紮八，宗亨恐分其功，不聽，而縱軍士取賊所棄資囊人畜而自有之。

translations.literal: The Yidu meng'an wished to pursue Kuoli and Zhaba with his own command; Zongheng, fearing his merit would be divided, did not permit it, but let soldiers take for themselves the rebels' abandoned goods, bags, livestock, and property.
translations.idiomatic: The Yidu meng'an wanted to chase Kuoli and Zhaba with his own men; Zongheng, fearing shared credit, refused—and instead let his soldiers help themselves to the rebels' abandoned baggage and livestock.

sentences.zh: 括裏、紮入由是得亡去，遂奔于宋。

translations.literal: Kuoli and Zhaba thereby were able to escape and flee, then fled to Song.
translations.idiomatic: Kuoli and Zhaba thus escaped and fled to the Song.

sentences.zh: 宗亨降甯州剌史。

translations.literal: Zongheng was demoted to Prefect of Ning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zongheng was demoted to prefect of Ning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其後，宋李世輔用括裏、紮八，遂取宿州，頗為邊患。

translations.literal: Afterward, Song's Li Shipu employed Kuoli and Zhaba, then took Suzhou, and they became quite a border menace.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Song general Li Shipu employed Kuoli and Zhaba to capture Suzhou, and they became a serious border threat.

sentences.zh: 神獨斡除同知安化軍節度使，稍合住除同知震武軍節度使事。

translations.literal: Shenduwo was appointed Associate Military Commissioner of Anhua Army; Shahezhu was appointed Associate Military Commissioner of Zhenwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Shenduwo was made associate military commissioner of Anhua Army; Shahezhu associate military commissioner of Zhenwu Army.

sentences.zh: 大定六年，點檢司奏，親軍中有逆黨子弟，請一切罷去。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dading, the Inspectorate memorialized that among the personal guard army were descendants of rebel faction members, requesting that all be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 6 (1166) the Inspectorate reported that the imperial guard contained descendants of rebel families and requested their wholesale dismissal.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「身預逆黨者罷之，餘勿問。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "Those who personally participated in the rebel faction shall be dismissed; the rest, do not investigate."
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: "Dismiss only those who took part in the rebellion; leave the rest alone."

sentences.zh: 贊曰：金人以燕山與宋，遂啟張覺跳樑之心，覺豈為宋者哉，蓋欲乘時以徼利耳。

translations.literal: The commentary says: The Jin gave Yan Mountain to the Song, thereby opening Zhang Jue's mind to vault the beam; was Jue truly for the Song? He merely wished to seize the moment and grasp profit.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: By ceding the Yan Mountains to the Song, the Jin gave Zhang Jue the idea of playing both sides—yet Jue was no friend of the Song; he simply meant to seize the moment for profit.

sentences.zh: 耶律余睹從宗望追天祚，曾不遺餘力，功成驕溢，自取誅滅，咈哉。

translations.literal: Yelü Yudu followed Zongwang in pursuing Tianzuo, exerting himself without reserve; when success came he grew proud and excessive and brought execution upon himself—how perverse!
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Yudu followed Zongwang in hunting down Emperor Tianzuo with unstinting zeal—then, swollen with pride at his success, brought ruin on himself. How perverse!

sentences.zh: 正隆佳兵，契丹作難，《傳》曰：「夫兵猶火也，弗戢將自焚。

translations.literal: Zhenglong prized arms; the Khitan raised trouble. The Commentary says: "Military affairs are like fire; if one does not restrain them, they will burn oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing glorified war, and the Khitan rose in revolt. As the Commentary says: "War is like fire—if you do not restrain it, it burns you.
